title: 学子故事 | 葛陆原，从你所爱，莫听蝉鸣
content:
Please Scroll up for English Version

Luyuan Ge: 2020 Graduate from the School of International Communications (IC), UNNC
Postgraduate Study: Taxonomy, Biodiversity and Evolution, Imperial College London
 
Taxonomy, biodiversity and evolution focus on the study of contemporary taxonomic techniques to analyse the status and trends of biodiversity. It is in fact very similar to the study of science and the basic requirements are almost the same as other professional programmes at Imperial College. Probably after studying this programme I can be a scientific or field researcher for animal taxonomy and conservation. Another possibility is to work in the media focusing on wildlife, so the combination of IC and this postgraduate programme is very valuable.

I have always loved wildlife and have been very concerned about nature conservation since I was a child, but I didn't connect my future with this interest. After entering UNNC, I had the opportunity to work in a bird sanctuary in India as an overseas volunteer through AIESEC. After comparing this experience with my following internships, I realised that I would like to work in the wilderness. I have made up my mind.

I did not encounter many difficulties when I applied for this programme. However, after I succeeded in moving from social to natural sciences I was still quite unsure of what to do, especially because I lacked the relevant knowledge in molecular biology, phylogenetics and programming. I do realise that I have to make good use of my vacation to better equip myself.
My parents were worried at first as it is so unrealistic to talk about future directions based solely on interests. I did not dare to think about it at first, but I had no interests in other work, so I was struggling and anxious for a while. Later on, I spent a lot of my spare time on activities related to this field and my professional skills have gradually improved. As a result, I embraced more opportunities such as national bird competitions, scientific research, and species surveys. I was finally able to chart my own path to the future. My parents are happy that I have found what I love, and I have their support.

I am one of the founders of NottinGreen Student Society and I am the leader of the Ecology Group. NottinGreen is a group of friends who affirm my values, give me encouragement and offer me a platform to express myself. I have also had the opportunity to meet important birdwatching partners and get to do a lot of things I wouldn't have the motivation to do alone, such as organising the university’s species list and participating in various birdwatching trips. Some UNNC students might remember that the site of the new library used to be a small forest, and I was also involved in helping to organise the bird species descriptions on the outside wall of the construction site when the new library was under construction.
UNNC allowed me to get in touch with high level wildlife workers who had an important influence on my future plans.

Overseas internships opened the door of nature observation for me and there were not many places that could provide such opportunities; and I do like the learning methods at UNNC — we have a lot of time for free exploration. Because of the strong international element around us, my classmates were all more individualistic and less "realistic" in their thinking, which gave me a very comfortable environment for free development.

In fact, when I first entered UNNC, I was in the School of Economics which is known for offering the highest starting salary for graduates of the FHSS. However, as a social science student it was impossible for me to transfer to a natural science programme such as Environmental Science. Therefore, I didn't try to do so at that time. I finally chose the School of International Communications which has more autonomy and is connected with the BBC, WWF, International Bird Federation and other dream jobs.

In addition, IC’s exchange rate (about 98%) gave me the opportunity to spend a year in the university’s UK campus where I gained a lot of valuable experience. In the UK, where the programme of nature observation originally appeared, it was easy for me to make a lot of foreign friends with the same interests in bird observing. I enjoyed the chance to go out with friends who share my interests, which I rarely experienced before when I was alone in China. I have also taken part in a number of local animal rescues, monitoring and conservation projects, all of which were very eye-opening and helped me develop new skills. Upon my return to China, I became more confident in myself to actively interact with people with the same interests, and the outcome of becoming more positive was more opportunities opened up for me.
IC is an interdisciplinary programme and requires good time management skills to balance my interests and study. The first point is to seek the common ground. As IC is a platform for cultivating international talent, I have set my goal as targeting international conservation organisations such as the WWF and the International Birding Federation which will maintain my motivation to continue studying in this programme. The next point is to constantly motivate myself to make learning “interesting”. Observing wild animals is my hobby and compared with other entertainment activities, I always want to go out to observe wild animals on suitable days.

I have done a lot of practical work, whether it is personal nature observation in my free time, or internship-oriented wildlife conservation, working as a research assistant, or taking part in bird watching tournaments and regional species survey projects held in China. All of these have made me more determined in my choice, helped me recognise my own limitations, and improve my professionalism through targeted learning.

I have two memorable internship experiences. The first one is rescuing amphibians which awaken from their hibernacula and return to their ponds to breed in the spring. NottinGreen organised volunteers to help collect hibernacula, including the great toad and the UK's priority conservation, great crested European salamander, and sent them to their breeding grounds. This means such slow-moving animals are not run over as they crossed the road. Another experience is monitoring barn owls. The barn owl is a popular owl in the UK as they help farmers catch many rodents, which is a very important part of the ecosystem. There was an old man in Nottingham who was a barn owl monitor. Every year he would bring some university students and others to put numbered anklets on all the adult barn owls and their babies around the farm and measure their weight and wingspan. I do hope that in the future the protection of animals in China can be more standardised. There are many amphibians living in mountain roads in some well-known attractions. However, every spring and summer, especially after the rain, the ground is covered with their carcasses. This is really heart breaking.
Bird watching gives me the feeling of seeing the world through binoculars in high-definition. It also gives me the pleasure of "adding new species" after recording those new members. Bird watching is very random, and the birds you meet depend on the season, habitat, altitude and luck. It's rewarding to find your target bird species in one place; and if you have a camera you can take good pictures which is also fascinating.

For the time being, I'm jus ‘taking one step and looking around before taking another’. I would like to decide on a career path after I have enough expertise to make an informed choice. To be honest, anything related wildlife and conservation is very desirable for me. After graduation, the current idea is to do a PhD. And after studying broad taxonomy, I’d like to focus on birds or amphibian reptiles for further study.


选择国际传播学(IC)除了人文关怀 还会有怎样的未来？
野生动物保护与IC 又会碰撞出怎样的火花？
今天就让我们跟随一位钟情于大自然的IC学长
一起探索他跨界的心路历程吧！

葛陆原
2020届国际传播学系毕业生
即将去帝国理工的分类学、生物多样性与进化专业就读研究生
NottinGreen (诺丁绿)学生社团组织创始人之一

Taxonomy, Biodiversity and Evolution 专业主要集中在对当代分类学技术的学习，以此来分析生物多样性的现状、走向等，是个十分偏理科的专业。未来的方向大概是动物分类向、保护向的科研或实地调查团队，和国际传播系也有着一定的契合度，比如可以从事 BBC 的野生动物媒体工作者等。

其实自己从小就喜欢野生动物，也比较关注自然保护。就像一个单纯喜欢看百科和动物世界的人一样，当时并没有想过把自己的未来和自然联系在一起。大学之后通过AIESEC（一个负责海外实习的社团组织）选择了相关方向的海外志愿者项目，去印度的鸟类保护区工作，一下打开了自然观察的大门。在经历了几次与自然保护无关的实习后，觉得自己不愿意去做一个生活一潭死水的“社会人”，还是野外能让自己快乐有活力，渐渐就下定决心了。

在申请这个专业的时候其实没有遇到多少阻力，英国研究生的申请比较的人性化，除了学术成绩也看重实践经历。本科期间自己的“贪玩”可能成为了不错的经历背景。在做这样的一个决定之前，也是和父母尝试沟通过的，家里人一开始当然是认为我很不务正业的！因为一个只有兴趣的小白就说未来方向什么的太不现实了。后来就是花了很多自己的业余时间去进行相关领域的活动，随着水平的提高也有越来越多的优质机会比如全国鸟赛、科研、物种调查摆在眼前。就这样自己做的事情逐渐能勾画出一条未来的路，家里人也渐渐开始理解自己的决定。现在他们为我找到所爱而庆幸，全力支持！
做海岛燕鸥环志
在读期间，应朋友的号召，大家联合创立了NottinGreen社团，后担任生态组的leader。社团会有很多人肯定自己的价值追求，给予我鼓励，给我提供了一个表达自己的平台。我也有机会在这里遇到了自己重要的观鸟伙伴，可以去做很多一个人没有动力去做的事情，比如整理学校的物种名录，很多观鸟行程等等。年级较高的同学应该记得，现在图书馆新馆的场地从前是一片小树林，当时为了纪念小树林，还参与了鸟类物种的整理，和几位同学一起推出了名为'Birds in UNNC'的艺术作品展，以此纪念曾经在这片土地上生活的生灵，纪念它们和UNNC一起度过的13年时光。

宁诺所提供的平台，使我能接触到很高水平的野生动物领域工作者，还是给我的未来规划带来了很重要的影响的；海外志愿者的氛围为我打开了自然观察的大门，虽然当时真的只是抱着体验的态度去海外保护区工作，但能找到这种机会的地方确实不多；最后表白下宁诺的学习模式，自由探索的时间很多。身边因为国际化元素浓厚，同学们也都比较有个性，想法没那么“现实”，算是给了我一个很舒适的自由发展环境吧。
NottinGreen当中2020届毕业生们与副校长合影

其实我入学的时候，选择的是人文社科学院毕业生起薪最高的经济系。当时是想作为一个文科生在国内应该是没法转到环科这样的理科专业的，所以当时就没有做转过去的尝试（现在比较后悔，觉得至少应该试试），而是选择了自主性较强、又能和 BBC、WWF （世界自然基金会）、国际鸟盟等一众梦幻岗位联系起来的国际传播系。

此外， IC 98%交换率让我有机会去英诺交换一年，在那里收获了非常多的宝贵经历。在英国这样一个自然观察起源级别的国家，自己很容易在观鸟的途中结识不少志同道合的外国朋友。之后我的英国自然观察行就变成了一部蹭车史，总是能和圈内的朋友一起出去，这是之前在国内孤军奋战的我很少能体验到的。我也由此参加了不少当地的动物救助、监测和保育，都是很开拓眼界和磨炼技术的事情。回国之后自己也就更有自信去积极地和圈内人交流了，而积极的结果就是更多的机会。

IC和这个学科跨度很大，需要很好的时间管理才能兼顾二者。一方面IC 是培养国际交流人才的平台，于是我一开始就把目标定位在了 WWF，国际鸟盟之类的国际保护组织，这样就会有继续学习本专业的动力是。另一方面观察野生动物本就是自己的爱好，天气合适的日子总是会想出去进行观察，代替了不少其他的娱乐活动。也因为自己的兴趣，会去积极进入这个领域的圈子，因此获得了不少宝贵的机会，有时候一个项目就可以短时间内跟在领域大咖后面学到很多。


<< 滑动查看葛陆原摄影作品>

为了找到自己的方向，我做了不少尝试，不论是空闲时的个人自然观察，还是实习向的野生动物保护、科研助手，亦或是国内举办的观鸟赛、地区性物种调查项目。这些都让我更加坚定，也认识到自己的局限性，想通过针对性的学习来提高自己的专业水平。

印象比较深刻的几次亲密接触，一次是救助两栖动物。春季是两栖类从冬眠地苏醒，返回池塘繁殖的季节，当时就是作为诺丁汉两栖爬行类组的成员，组织志愿者帮助收集冬眠地的两栖类动物，包括大蟾蜍和英国重点保护的大冠欧螈，送它们去繁殖地，避免这些行动缓慢的动物在过马路的时候被碾压。讲到这点，就想到我国目前两栖类丰富的地区，每到春夏，尤其雨后，山间公路就是横尸遍野，也是挺让人心疼的。

另一次也是在英诺交换做志愿者的时候对仓鸮的监测。仓鸮是英国人民很喜爱的猫头鹰，它们会帮助农场主捕捉很多鼠类，是生态链中很重要的一环，所以春夏之交仓鸮产仔的季节，对它们的数量监测就很重要。当时诺丁汉有一个做仓鸮监测的老人，每年会带一些大学生或者野生动物相关人士给农场周边的仓鸮成鸟和宝宝戴上有编号的脚环，测量体重翼展等。那是我第一次亲身实践保育项目，也是第一次和野生猛禽近距离接触。

关于观鸟带给我的感受，这是个可以通过望远镜能看到纪录片感的高清世界，记录到个人的新种之后又会有种“加新”的快乐。而且观鸟这件事随机性很强，能遇到什么鸟跟季节、生境、海拔、运气都有很大关系，在一个地方找到自己的目标鸟种是很有成就感的事情，鸟的种数增加也就有点像自己收藏夹里的内容物越来越多一样。最后就是，如果有相机的话，拍出好的照片也是个追求。
观鸟赛参赛经历
01
山西沁园全国观鸟赛创新奖 
02
神农架全国观鸟赛 挑战突破奖
03
鄱阳湖国际观鸟赛的优胜奖第二名、至尊鸟种奖

鄱阳湖观鸟比赛中英小队

葛陆原表示，只要是涉及野外和保护的工作都很令人憧憬。对于未来规划，暂时想着走一步看一步，在有足够的专业知识支持之后再决定工作的方向。毕业后目前的想法是读博，在学完广义的分类学之后，细化到鸟类或者两栖爬行类分支继续深造。

听完葛同学的分享，相信大家对于IC的可塑性有了新的认知，也对自己的生涯规划有了更多想法。期待大家都可以寻找到自己所爱的专业并坚定地走下去，也祝福他可以在野生动物的相关领域有更多的收获！

title: 理工优秀校友专访 | 师慧：坚定地选择，进而全力以赴，去追逐自己的光
content:
03
校友故事

师慧， 2014级建筑环境与能源应用工程学生，在校期间年级排名始终保持在前5%，并且连续三年获得Dean's Scholarship，2018年以一等学位毕业。同年，考入伦敦大学学院Environmental Design and Engineering专业。目前就职于骏业建筑科技（上海）有限公司，是一名绿色建筑工程师。


永远保持学习和思考的能力
在UNNC的四年，师慧自律性极强，无论是专业课还是文化课，都给自己制定了具体的学习计划，这也是她成绩能常年名列前茅并且取得奖学金的原因。“我一般会利用开学前的几周空闲时间预习一下这学期的lecture，或者整理一些笔记。因为在各种essay和coursework来了之后，你基本没有时间看PPT做笔记了。

此外，师慧强调对考试试题的整理归纳很重要。因为每门课都会有past paper，你大概会知道老师会考什么题型，形式是什么样子的。最重要的一点，在学习中，无论做什么事情，都要缜密，有逻辑。”

师慧的严谨与缜密也被她很好地运用到了工作当中，“工作中，我会不断向有项目经验的同事学习，认真完成好自己手上的工作，在过程中培养起自己对不同类型项目的理解和对这个行业的全方位的认知和规划。当然，保有学生时代的学习和思考状态也非常重要。”

师慧表示目前的工作是她回国后通过社招面试找到的，主要负责新旧国标的标识申报，参与LEED和WELL项目。从学校到职场，她适应地很自如，“我很喜欢这份工作，绿色建筑是建筑行业未来的趋势，学校学习的内容可以用上一部分，着手工作不会很陌生和困难；而且工作内容相对比较轻松。”

事实上，作为一名绿建工程师所需的时刻反思复盘与不断学习超越的精神，恰好与她的内心有某种契合之处。“对项目的统筹和处理问题的方式会是工作中很重要的一部分。在工作中一定会犯一些大大小小的错误，我觉得都是正常的，如果能每一次都吸取教训，认真思考，未来随着项目经验的积累，这些经历会变得很宝贵。”诚如是，保持学习的状态，从工作中吸取经验并将其转化成自我成长的养分，一直是她孜孜以求的。

较真，对于自己的考验和考试
在采访中我们了解到，在校期间，除去大三去英国交换，其余三年师慧和小伙伴们共同创办了一家义工游学机构，当时她负责整个欧洲项目。师慧的大学生活有着AB两面，一面是热血追梦的理想少年，一面是能力超凡的职场新星。她在保持着专业前5%的同时，也完美地平衡了工作，表面看似轻松，实际上她私下却没少花功夫。

“其实大二的时候都是非常忙碌的，一方面学术压力很大，要准备交换的事宜，另一方面自己也有很多的繁琐的工作要处理，我曾有一段时间很累很迷茫，几乎完全没有自己的时间去做自己想做的事情，不知道自己究竟想要什么，也不明白工作的意义在哪里。”

工作和学习的高压使得师慧偶尔也会怀疑自己，但她很快就能调节好自己的心态重新出发，“一旦我闲下来，我就总想找点事情做。所以我觉得工作是我生活中不可或缺的一部分。只要你平衡好工作和学习的时间，提升效率，这些困难你都是可以战胜的。总之要调整好每天的心态，不要总抱怨，因为抱怨并不能解决问题，每天积极开心一点，心态好了，生活就顺利了。”

师慧有着自己较真和不安分的一面，她的内心隐藏着一股蓬勃的能量。说白了内心驱动力还是想证明自己，如何保持两者的平衡，可以做到什么样的程度，是师慧对于自己的考验和考试。而最后随之而来的每一份掌声和荣耀，她都实打实地接住了。



坚定地选择，不要退而求其次
2018年，师慧曾在另一段采访中表示自己未来想去上海工作，“因为上海有很多外资企业，很适合中外合作办学大学毕业的学生。其次，我的朋友们大部分都会去北上广工作，人脉圈也不会断。”而后，她为自己曾经的选择全力以赴，心无旁骛，果真实现了自己的理想，没有被现实束缚半分。

“先明确自己想要的是什么，比如更关注薪资、工作环境还是工作氛围等，在面试的时候也可以大胆的向对方公司提出自己想要了解的信息，才有机会找到一份也许不是最好，但相对符合自己个人气质的工作。”

因为坚持做自己，因为知道自己要什么而努力，双重的坚韧与执着才构成了师慧如今的百炼成钢。“希望我们在成长的路中，都越来越知道自己想要的是什么，并且朝着那束光，慢慢走过去。”

谈及对学弟学妹的建议，师慧说道，“还是要好好珍惜自己的大学时光，要努力学习，最后获得一个令人满意的结果，这样你才不会后悔。要用大一大二的时间多做一些有意义的事情，去丰富自己的人生，譬如支教，譬如实习。也要时刻关注一下我们学校的邮件，这里面有很多很好的机会，一定不要错过。还有就是一定要提升好英语，多去找一些练习的机会，最好找一些小伙伴和你一起学习。”
这一年，从校园到职场，师慧一路不停歇，走得昂首阔步。她说大学四年“能交到很好的朋友，认识一群有共同语言的人”就已是莫大的幸运。“该享受的青春还是要尽情享受的，遇到困难该走的路也还是要坚持走下去的。”虽然青春路上纵有迷茫，但脚踏实地的师慧说出这话时，也有自豪的语气。

Hui Shi is a graduate of 2018 Architectural Environment Engineering (AEE) Programme. During her colleague life, Hui kept top 5% in the AEE programme and had received Dean’s Scholarship for three times. When she graduated, she was one of the five students who received First Class degree in the AEE programme. Following that, she went to University College London and pursued the PG study in the Environmental Design and Engineering. Currently, she has become a professional engineer in green building company base in Shanghai.

Hui is always a highly self-disciplined student and used to make detailed studying plan for herself. Before the start of one semester, she would preview the whole semester’s lecture and sort out the difficulties in the notebook. Then during the semester, when there were full of dues, she were able to check the past paper and get familiar to the examination. More importantly, she believes every detail matters.

During her four years study in the UNNC, she founded a company with her classmates. At that time, she admitted that there had been a period of time she was quite tired and once confused. But she adjusted herself quickly. “Since you can balance your time between work and study and be more efficient you can tackle with these problems.” She said.

Hui came back to China after graduating from UCL and got the job offer in a green building company in Shanghai. She works as a green building engineer and is responsible for the declaration of new and old GB identification, and LEED & WELL certified projects. From college to work, from student to professional engineer, Hui said she adapts quite well.

Green building is the trend in AEC industry. Every day she can learn new stuff from her work. Her previous education has laid sound foundation to her work but she keep learning the new technology in this industry. She encourages the young engineer that making mistakes is unavoidable as long as you can learn from it, which will become your treasure in the future.

“Work hard and play hard so that you well leave with no regret.” UNNC provides her a global platform to broaden her horizon and a truly global alumni network. She encourages all the UNNCers to dream big and enjoy the wonderful time with their friends.

title: Alumni Story | 熊梦格：三十而已，所有的付出都不会白费
content:
Xiong Mengge graduated with a Bachelor’s Degree in International Business with French from Nottingham University Business School China (NUBS China) in 2011 and gained her Master’s Degree in Management with specialisation in Marketing from ESCP Europe in 2014. She formerly worked in Paris for Lighthouse and Louis Vuitton, and currently works at the headquarter of Richemont Group in Geneva, Switzerland as the International Senior Chinese Business Development Manager of Piaget.

Scroll down to read her full story.
熊梦格，诺丁汉大学商学院（中国）2011届国际商务与法语专业本科毕业生。2014年于法国巴黎获得欧洲高等商学院ESCP Europe管理学硕士学位，市场营销学(Marketing - Branding)方向。曾在巴黎精品战略咨询公司LIGHTHOUSE和路易威登LOUIS VUITTON有过实习经历，之后进入全球第二大奢侈品集团历峰集团RICHEMONT GROUP总部工作六年，现在伯爵（PIAGET）总部（瑞士日内瓦）担任品牌全球中国业务拓展高级经理。伯爵创立于1874年，是历峰集团旗下著名的钟表珠宝品牌。

采访熊梦格约了一段时间，她很忙，经常出差，全球各地飞。约到一个下午，宁波连线瑞士日内瓦，我的采访、她的回忆，就此展开。
学生时代：“我生命中最美好的一些人都是在宁诺遇到的”
谈起母校，十年时光流逝如水，那段闪亮的青春仍清晰如昨。

2007年，高中毕业于安徽宣城中学的熊梦格成为了宁波诺丁汉大学（以下简称“宁诺”）的一员。父亲是她报考宁诺的头号支持者，他从事教育行业，曾在国家级教育学术交流中去到英国诺丁汉大学，一下喜欢上了这所学校。他常和女儿说，宁诺“和国外很像”“学术氛围特别好”。带着熊梦格实地参观后，父女俩一拍即合，将其作为第一志愿报考。
这里青空辽阔，长风万里，鸟儿们得以乘风振翅，高飞远翔。“我从没见过这样的地方。它总是鼓励你去主动思考——不管是在学习实践中有什么疑问，还是有什么兴趣和能力，选择什么课程和课外活动，或者是想在其他什么方面提升自己……你都要自己去想。学校会从方方面面为你提供指引和支持，帮你实现自己的想法。”熊梦格说。

除了自由的理念、强大的支持，这里还有她的良师益友与甜甜的初恋。“我生命中最美好的一些人都是在宁诺遇到的。”

她形容法语老师们有的风趣幽默，有的浪漫优雅，因为是小班教学，师生互动颇多，感情颇深，“既给了我很多学业上的指导，又让我对法国语言和文化产生了更深的兴趣。”辅导员尹星星老师则是一路陪伴她成长的知心哥哥，“他带我们不太像管理，而是很人性化，很愿意听我们的想法，沟通时也没有任何距离和架子。能够感受到，他在用心帮助我们成长。”

如果大学的回忆是本书，“伙伴”就是其中最柔软的一页。“人生中能遇到大学这帮朋友，真的很幸运，”熊梦格感慨道，“是他们让我成为了更好的人。”毕业后，虽然去了不同的国家，他们仍会在每年圣诞互相访问，结婚时也总会记得把好友叫来当伴娘。

熊梦格的丈夫就是她在宁诺的同窗好友，大一是同学，大二成为了朋友，大四在一起，毕业后和她一道赴法深造，现在在巴黎汇丰银行HSBC工作。时至今日，两人已携手走过近十年。“他是我的初恋。”熊梦格说，声波里都能感受到那份笑意、那份甜蜜。
2011年，熊梦格作为“优秀毕业生”从宁诺毕业，去往欧洲高等商学院（ESCP Europe）巴黎校区继续深造，它是全球最顶尖的商学院之一。熊梦格所申请的该校管理学硕士专业，2019年被英国《金融时报》评为全球第五名。她说，正是宁诺的国际化教育、英国交换项目等经历让她在申请者中脱颖而出，与注重跨文化背景的ESCP达成共鸣。
职场生活：挑战越多，成长越多
熊梦格在巴黎斩获了许多优质实习经历，其中包括当地品牌管理领域的精品咨询公司Lighthouse、世界第二大奢侈品集团历峰集团、知名奢侈品牌路易威登等等，她也常常因此受邀回到ESCP，为学弟学妹分享求职经验。她将其总结为：第一，要有清晰且切合实际的方向；第二，要在面试的准备上留足时间、下足功夫。“基本上所有的面试，我都会提前很久就开始准备，每一场都有十几页的准备材料。”
 
熊梦格对第一份实习的期待是，学到的东西越多越好。毕竟她在ESCP的细分专业是市场营销以及该分支下的品牌管理，从事这一方向需要大量实战经验。她进一步分析，与大型公司的市场营销部门相比，咨询机构对于实习生和正式工更加一视同仁，实习生能够深度参与具体的项目，其工作内容虽然更困难，但也更核心。于是熊梦格选择了品牌管理咨询领域的翘楚Lighthouse。在这里，她如愿得到了全面而快速的成长，尤其是在为某知名奢侈品公司重塑品牌形象的项目中，她的工作内容几乎深入覆盖了市场营销的所有领域，成为了求职历峰时最加分的经历。
从实习生转正的时候，熊梦格加入了历峰新开设的中国事务与战略部。她用五年的时间从分析员一路做到高级经理，与同伴齐力开疆拓土，发展新业务，吸纳新成员，使部门快速成长成熟，赢得了各品牌的认可和重视。熊梦格也与部门一同成长着，“在这里工作，只有抱着非常积极主动的态度，才能不畏怯责任和风险，不断地想出新点子，不断地做出新尝试。因为所有的东西都是新的，没有人告诉你应该做什么、借鉴什么。很多时候都是很难的。”
 
她工作时的状态和超人如出一辙——飞来飞去，锐不可当。一天之内和同事、上级、合作伙伴等人开七八个会是基本操作，两三天就换个国家出差更是家常便饭。身边的人心疼她，她却从没喊过累，“只要付出后能看到收获，辛苦根本不算什么。”
 
回想这一路，刚到法国时繁重的课业与文化的隔阂，初入历峰时高压的环境与艰难的探索，熊梦格说，这些经历教会了她：挑战越多，成长越多。“所以每当很苦的时候，我都知道，只要我坚持下去，这些努力就不会白白付出。”
毕竟，即使付出没有收获成功，但付出一定会收获成长。正如正如约翰·麦斯威尔所言：“Sometimes you win, sometimes you learn.”「人生不是得到，就是学到。」
正确看待奢侈品
熊梦格从事的是奢侈品行业。奢侈品在经济学上讲，指的是价值/品质关系比值最高的产品。在生活当中，奢侈品牌享有很特殊的市场和社会地位。从另外一个角度上看(如市场营销学)，奢侈品又是指无形价值/有形价值关系比值最高的产品。近期热播的电视剧《三十而已》，引发了大家有不少关于奢侈品的讨论。我们聊及怎样定义奢侈品，个人持怎样的态度。熊梦格坦言她自己也是机缘巧合进了这个行业，她说道：奢侈品这个词其实更多展示的是世人对它的解读，但奢侈二字却并不总给人带来正面的态度，比如从汉字架构上来看就既有“大”又有“多”，让人感觉是一种于己不称的浪费和挥霍；这却不是这个行业真正受人追崇并传承百年背后的奥妙，所以我们在行业内更喜欢用的是“精品”这个词：精品工业Luxury Industry和精品世家Luxury Maison。精在哪里：精湛在钟表师一家几代在瑞士的静谧山谷里十年如一日地做着同一个细小零件的打磨和制作，精湛在这些作品都承载了工匠艺人世代相传的手工艺并且在如此工业化的社会坚持手工完成，也精湛在始终致力于给所有喜爱世家和他们作品的人们一个最纯粹的体验：让你感受工匠技艺和精密机械魅力，享受极致的美。
熊梦格说她最近也看了这部剧，她最深的感受就是 - 要学会跟最真实的自己对话，尊重“她”，解放“她”。人类都是社会性动物，自然而然会被社会的“价值观”所影响和负累，剧中顾佳千辛万苦变卖资产想通过H家限量款包包打入的圈子其实根本不是属于她的圈子，不是财力，而是她们坚持的东西和想要的东西是不同的。而我们现在其实越来越多的能看到奢侈品消费人群已经开始趋向于真正品牌想要触碰到的受众：那些欣赏品牌工艺，喜欢品牌风格并乐于诠释它的那些人。在选择你的下一款包包/珠宝/腕表时，不要为它所累，而是要在对品牌内涵真正的认同感中让它呈现出你最好最美的那一面！

在和欧洲人工作生活时间久了之后，熊梦格越来越能感受到欧洲人自我意识的成熟之处，他们习惯于跟自己对话，了解自己真正想要的东西，不惧尝试，乐于体验，为自己而活；而许多的欧洲品牌也是如此，数百年来这些品牌的诞生和发展都不是为了卖高价，而是经历了千锤百炼出来的每一件作品和传承百年的品牌信念让它有了那些应有的价值。

最后，希望这个行业的存在可以带你去到那个自己想去的地方，感受自己想要的满足感，学会更多地取悦自己，而不是取悦他人。
寄语学弟学妹
“我看到有的学弟学妹总是很急，想要马上进入到下一个阶段。我觉得每个阶段都是最好的阶段，都是不能重来的、需要好好珍惜的。活在当下，认真学习，去交朋友，去充实自己，去做那些你想做的事情。只要你在这段时间里充分地利用、充分地享受了，你后面的路一定会自然而然地走好的。尤其在宁诺这样一个特别美好的地方——我们毕业的人常常会想，怎么会有这么象牙塔的地方存在！你应该尽情地享受在这里的时光才对。”


Xiong Mengge: No effort made is ever in vain

Xiong Mengge graduated with a Bachelor’s Degree in International Business with French from Nottingham University Business School China (NUBS China) in 2011 and gained her Master’s Degree in Management with specialisation in Marketing from ESCP Europe in 2014. She formerly worked in Paris for Lighthouse and Louis Vuitton, and currently works at the headquarters of Richemont Group in Geneva, Switzerland as the International Senior Chinese Business Development Manager of Piaget. Founded in 1874, Piaget is a famous watch and jewellery brand owned by Richemont, the world’s second-largest luxury goods company.

Scheduling an interview with Xiong Mengge took some time since she is often busy making business trips around the world. On a free afternoon, the interview took place virtually, connecting Ningbo with Geneva, Switzerland. See below for our interview with Mengge.
Slide up for more details.
Days at university: Met the best people in my life
Though her days at UNNC lie long in the past, in retrospect this bright period of her formative years remains clear as if they happened yesterday.

In 2007, Mengge, from Xuancheng, Anhui Province, was admitted into the University of Nottingham Ningbo China (UNNC). Her father is her best supporter, helping her apply to UNNC. As someone in the education industry, he once visited the University of Nottingham in the UK in a national English teaching networking event and discovered this “treasure” of a university. He comments that UNNC “resembles universities in the UK” and “has an excellent academic atmosphere”. After visiting the university on-site with his daughter, they fitted in easily and decided to apply for it as the first choice.

The campus unfolds with vast greenery and soaring birds. “I’ve never seen such a place. UNNC always encourages you to think actively about whether you have any questions about your studies or practice, what interests and abilities you have, what courses or extracurricular activities you want to choose, or what else you want to improve on, etc. You have to think for yourself. The university will provide you with much guidance and support to help you achieve what you want,” Mengge said.

In addition to the philosophy of freedom and firm support, there are also excellent teachers and friends. “The best people in my life I met while at UNNC,” Mengge said.

She described the teachers who taught her French as humorous, idealists and sophisticated. Due to the small-size seminars, teachers and students actively interact with each other and build close relationships. “They not only gave me a lot of guidance in my studies, but they also made me much more interested in the French language and culture.” Yin Xingxing, her Student Support Advisor, was always with her. “She did not treat us with a managerial attitude, but in a very humanised and approachable way, and was willing to carefully listen to our views. We felt that she wanted to help us.”

If memories of UNNC were like a book, then friendships were the best chapter. “I’m so lucky to have these friends in my life. It is they who made me into a better person.” After graduation, although we have moved to different countries, we still visit each other every Christmas and accept invitations to be bridesmaids when getting married.

Mengge’s husband was also one of her friends at UNNC. He went to France with Mengge after graduation for further study and now works for HSBC in Paris. The couple has been with each other for nearly a decade. “He is my first love,” Mengge said with a contented smile.

In 2011, Mengge graduated as an “Outstanding Graduate” from UNNC and went on to study at ESCP Europe in Paris, which is one of the top business schools in the world. Its Master in Management programme, which Mengge was enrolled in, is ranked 5th worldwide in the 2019 Financial Times Master in Management rankings. According to Mengge, it was the international education, the exchange programme to the UK campus and other opportunities provided by UNNC that made her stand out among other applicants for this programme, which prefers students with cross-cultural backgrounds.

Career path: The more challenges, the more growth
Mengge completed many excellent internships in Paris, including the consulting firm Lighthouse, Richemont Group and Louis Vuitton. As a result, she is often invited back to ESCP to share her job hunting experience. She summed it up as first, have a clear and realistic goal; and second, spend sufficient time and effort on preparing for interviews. “For almost every interview, I prepared in advance with dozens of pages of materials.”

Mengge’s expectation for her first internship was that the more she could learn from it, the better. After all, she specialises in marketing, and more specifically, brand management, a career path that requires a lot of practice. She further analysed that in comparison with the marketing department in big companies, consulting agencies treat interns and permanent employees equally. Interns are thus able to participate deeply in specific projects. Although tasks in these agencies are often more difficult, they are more essential as well. Therefore, Mengge chose Lighthouse, a leader in the field of brand management consulting. This choice proved to be a wise one. She comprehensively and rapidly improved as she expected, especially in a project that had to provide research and a complete analysis of a luxury company to help its rebranding. Her work in it almost covered all the fields of marketing and became the most eye-catching experience when she later applied for Richemont’s position.

In 2015, Mengge joined Richemont’s newly established China Affairs and Strategy Department. She spent five years making her way from a project analyst to a senior manager, and worked jointly with her colleagues to develop new business and recruit new members. The new department has grown rapidly and has won recognition and attention from various brands. Mengge has also improved a lot. “In this department, only with a very proactive attitude can I keep up with new ideas and make new attempts without being afraid of taking responsibilities and risks. Because everything is new here, and no one tells you what to do or who to learn from, we usually had a hard time.”

She works in the same way as superman does — flying around, full of vigour. It’s normal for her to have eight meetings with colleagues, superiors and business partners in a day, or to make a business trip to a different country every two days. However, she never admits that she is tired, “As long as I can see good results after making a big effort, hard work is not a big deal.”

Looking back at the heavy workloads and cultural barriers she faced when she first entered ESCP, as well as the high-pressure environment and the difficult time when she first entered Richemont, Mengge said these experiences have taught her that challenges stimulate improvement. “So whenever it was tough, I know for sure that if I hold on more and persevere, none of it will be in vain.”

After all, although perseverance may not bring success, it will bring improvement. As John Maxwell said, “Sometimes you win; sometimes you learn.”

Luxury goods: Quality matters
Mengge works in the luxury industry. From an economics standpoint, luxury goods refer to products that have the highest cost-to-quality ratio. In daily life, luxury brands, with their unique places in the market, represent social status. On the other hand, if seen from a marketing perspective, luxury goods are also the products that have the highest intangible value to tangible value ratio. According to Wikipedia, in economics, a luxury good (or upmarket good) is a good for which demand increases more than proportionally as income rises, so that expenditures on the good become a greater proportion of overall spending. Luxury goods contrast with necessity goods, in which demand increases proportionally less than income. A recent popular TV drama, Nothing But Thirty, created a stir about luxury goods on social media.

In the interview, we also discussed how to define the term ‘luxury’, and what Mengge’s attitude is towards luxury goods. Mengge explained that she entered the industry by chance, and said, “The term shechipin (luxury goods) reflects the people’s understanding of luxury, but the word often does not come across positively because it can exhibit a sense of waste and extravagance. Such a perception does not align with the historical nature of the industry, so we prefer to use the word jingpin (Luxury Goods) as in jingpin gongye (Luxury Industry) and jingpin shijia (Luxury Maison/Brand). Exquisiteness lies in the careful and persistent craftwork by generations of Swiss horologist, and their choice of handcraft in an increasingly industrialised society brings about a pure and elegant balance between craftsmanship and precision machinery.”

After watching Nothing But Thirty, Mengge indicated that her deepest reflection is that we need to learn to talk with our truest selves, giving ourselves respect and freedom. People are social beings, so we are often influenced and pressured by societal values. In the drama, the heroine Gu Jia tries with great effort to buy a limited edition luxury bag in order to enter into a social class that she does not belong to. In truth, what differentiates them is not their spending power, but the value they hold and look for in goods. Alternate consumers of luxury goods are becoming the ones that brands actually want to reach for—those who appreciate craftsmanship and enjoy the expressing the brands’ styles. Next time when you choose your luxury bag, jewellery, or watch, be sure to understand and appreciate the value behind the brand to see the true beauty of the piece, instead of being pressured to buy the luxury item.

After working and living with Europeans for a while, Mengge has learnt about the maturity of their self-awareness: they self-reflect to understand what they really want and enjoy experiencing different things to live for themselves. Similarly, many European brands are established not to sell a high price, but to honour the historical value behind each created piece.

To UNNCers
“I see some students are always in a hurry to move on to the next stage. In my opinion, every stage is the best stage as they can’t be lived over again. Cherish each stage, live in the moment, study hard, make friends, enrich yourself, and do those things that you want to do. As long as you make the most of the moment and enjoy yourself, the road ahead will take care of itself. Especially in a place as glorious as UNNC — we alumni often wonder how such a university could exist! You should enjoy your time here.”

title: 宁诺暑期放大招：170余项科研实习项目，42名导师自愿留校指导
content:
Please scroll down for the English version - FoSE Undergraduate Summer Research Replacement receives great popularity among students.

酷暑天，宁波诺丁汉大学理工实验室里一片繁忙景象。600余名理工科学生选择留在校园，参与暑期学生体验项目。今年仅科研实习项目数量就多达170余项，42名导师自愿留校带领学生进行暑期课题研究。这是宁波诺丁汉大学理工学院自开设暑期项目以来，规模最大，参与人数最多的一次。

作为暑期短学期项目的一部分，暑期项目旨在为在校生搭建与来自不同学科、不同年级学生接触与互动，了解科学研究实质，增进科研技能，探索自身兴趣的平台。考虑到疫情影响，学院还人性化地开设了线上远程科研项目，为国际生与交换生们提供参与科研的机会。

化学专业的大二学生沈书恒加入的是唐本灿老师指导的计算化学科研项目。这个研究项目是利用DFT方法在Gaussian软件（一个仿真计算化学软件）中计算环加成反应。在参与暑期科研项之前，沈书恒也一直以为化学是一门重视实验和分析的学科，而在接触到计算化学之后，他却感受到现代化学研究已经离不开理论和数据计算。

他说，暑研开始至今，唐本灿老师指导他们如何构建出较简单的模拟底物，再通过计算得到模拟底物反应的各种数据，例如热力学数据，键长键角数据，然后利用这些数据计算真实反应，简化了直接计算真实反应的难度。而这样的过程，让他觉得很有意思并产生了研究兴趣。


同样从探索未知中打开新世界大门的还有来自数学系的大三学生陆米然。她连续两年跟随的暑期导师是专注环境科学领域的Faith Chan博士。课题是宁波市蓝绿色基础设施与海绵城市建设调查研究。“这两年暑假我几乎逛遍了宁波大大小小的公园，采集数据，然后进行数据分析。我很享受这个过程，完全不觉得枯燥，而且越来越喜欢环境科学这个学科，甚至想过往这个方向申研。”

Faith Chan是自愿留下带领学生进行暑期科研的老师之一。当被问及为什么愿意义务带领学生做暑期课题时，Faith表示希望给到学生机会去接触科研、学习新的知识。这点也得到电气与电子工程系的Chiew-Foong Kwong博士的认同，他的研究领域集中在5G通讯技术，尤其是使用机器学习技术来解决移动管理和移动设备缓存的问题。“在我的项目中，学生可以接触到最前沿的5G通讯技术的发展。”


据了解，暑期科研实习项目设立之初，理工学院就希望能通过阅读文献、探讨问题、户外考察、采集数据、撰写报告等，让学生有机会沉浸式体验科研的全过程，将自己在课堂所学的知识应用到实际生产和生活之中。经过几年的磨合和探索，我们欣喜地看到不仅学生找到了兴趣所在和发展方向，暑研项目更是为导师们的科研注入了新的想法与观点。

“本科生的无穷创造力和对科研的热情给我留下了深刻的印象。” 理工学院地理科学系在读博士生徐宇尧说，去年暑假他和博士导师Faith Chan一起，带领着本科生考察宁波城市河流体系，从中获得了许多宝贵的帮助。建筑与建筑环境系Ali Cheshmehzangi博士此前带领的暑期科研团队所取得的研究成果还被收录在了国际核心期刊上。

另外，今年的暑期体验项目除科研实习项目外，还设有创新实验室、核心技能培训项目以及志愿活动与文化赏析的项目。这些项目既让学生掌握专业技能与实验室技能，也通过各类传统文化实践活动，让学生体悟“知行合一”，培养良好的人文素养。


FoSE Undergraduate Summer Research Replacement receives great popularity among students

The Undergraduate Summer Research Replacement programme this year has the largest number of participants since its establishment. Organised by the Faculty of Science Engineering (FoSE), the ongoing programme includes over 170 research projects; 42 tutors stayed on campus voluntarily to provide guidance, and more than 600 students participated. 

Aiming to stimulate students' interest in research, the programme provides them a platform to apply knowledge into the real-industry project and get them prepared for future academic and career development. 

In addition, considering the impact of the COVID-19, FoSE also launched an online remote research programme, which provides opportunities for international students and staff to participate in scientific research. 

Miran Lu, a year three student of Mathematics, has followed Dr Faith Chan, Associate Professor of Environmental Sciences, to conduct research on blue-green infrastructures and development of sponge city programme in Ningbo for two consecutive years. 

"During the past two summers, I have visited almost all the parks in Ningbo, collecting data and analysing the data. I enjoyed this process very much and like environmental sciences more and more. I even want to pursue a Master’s in this field," said Miran.  

Dr Chan is one of the tutors who volunteered to stay and instruct students to do the summer research. When speaking of his motivation of staying, he said that he wanted to give students the opportunity to practice scientific research and learn new knowledge. 

Through the summer research programme, FoSE hopes to provide students with the opportunity to experience the whole process of scientific from reading literature, discussing problems, outdoor investigation, data collection and report writing and enable them to practice in real life. 

The exploration and innovation of students has also provided inspiration for the tutors. The research outcomes of a summer research team led by Dr. Ali Cheshmehzangi of the Department of Architecture and Built Environment was accepted by a key international journal. 

In addition to the scientific research projects, this year's summer programme also includes innovation labs, core skills training programmes, volunteer activities and cultural appreciation programmes to cultivate diverse skills of students and enrich their extracurricular experience.

title: 这一封出自工业设计专业之手的录取通知书，你值得拥有
content:
Please scroll down for the English Version
 HELLO Is this your offer letter?
近日，宁波诺丁汉大学新生录取通知书揭开了神秘的面纱，一经亮相，就吸引了众人的视线。今年的录取通知书封面采用了分层设计的理念，采用宁诺的地标建筑钟楼为主体，颇具意趣。随着录取通知书到来的，还有一张由工业设计专业大四同学刘采妮自主设计的立体贺卡，以星空蓝为底色，全方位展现了钟楼的整体造型。
钟楼（Trent Building），是诺丁汉大学最重要的标志性建筑，在中国、英国和马来西亚三校都有相同的建筑。它的命名是为了向诺丁汉大学最大的捐助者 Lord Trent 表达敬意，他曾向诺丁汉大学捐赠了校园的建筑用地和10万英镑。在英国诺丁汉大学主校区University Park里，我们可以看到一栋历史更加悠久的钟楼，如今它已经拥有超过百年的历史了。
按顺时针，分别是英国诺丁汉大学主校区的春夏秋冬
马来西亚校区的钟楼

这也是为什么刘采妮同学选用钟楼，制成立体贺卡的原因。“钟楼是我们学校的标志性建筑，用钟楼更有代表性和纪念意义吧。每一次在回学校的路上，当我远远看到钟楼时，就会感到格外的亲切，仿佛像回到家一般。”相信每一位宁诺的学子，都会对钟楼留下特殊的回忆和感情。
美丽的UNNC校园
UNNC Campus
在贺卡上，还有宁波诺丁汉大学校长杨福家院士和执行校长尼克·迈尔斯教授的寄语，寄望新生在宁诺成为一名积极的学习者，在这所国际化的校园里解锁无限可能。
刘采妮同学是工业设计专业的学生，之前还为2019届毕业生设计了理工专属的毕业礼物。本次的立体贺卡沿用了去年毕业礼物的整体造型设计，对于钟楼的形状做了一些调整。经过几次改版之后，终于和厂家敲定了最终的设计方案。如果说有什么遗憾的地方的话，采妮表示，本来我们要选定的诺丁汉蓝，因为纸材质的限制，可能会有一些色差，不能很好地展现诺丁汉蓝。
2019届理工学院本科毕业生的毕业礼物
刘采妮同学在今年9月份就会进入大四的学习，她也祝福今年的新生可以在宁诺这个大家庭中，找到自己喜欢的生活和学习方式，了解自己真正想要什么，明确未来的方向。最重要的是，在未来的四年时光中，留下美好的回忆。

据悉，本周五，也就是今天下午，2020年第一批录取通知书将飞往它的“主人”。期待九月与你们相约在宁诺校园啦。

The design of 2020 new Gaokao recruitment student offer letter has refreshed people’s impression to it. Apart from the traditional offer letter, this year, we include a 3D greeting card in the shape of Trent Building, the most iconic building on campus.

Trent Building has become a symbol of University of Nottingham. It originates from the Trent Building in the University Park in the Nottingham UK. As University of Nottingham expanded overseas campus in the beginning of twenty-first century, like the University of Nottingham Malaysia, the China campus was also designed to mirror the attributes of University Park in the UK, with a lake and its own version of Nottingham Trent Building.

The 3D greeting card is designed by one of our talented Product Design and Manufacture (PDM) students Caini Liu, who is also the designer of the graduation gift for the FoSE Class of 2019. “Trent Building is so special for UNNCers. Every time I saw it, I felt like I am coming home.”

She will enter her final year in September. As a senior UNNCer and the designer of offer letter, she wish every fresher could enjoy their life in the UNNC and find their own interests.

title: 理工生修炼手册 | 王彦婷：厚积薄发，我在二进制的世界中，挖掘自身的无限潜力
content:
Please scroll down for the English version
王彦婷
2020届计算机科学毕业生
毕业高中：湖南省长郡中学
计算机科学专业2020届的毕业生王彦婷同学在宁诺四年的学习生涯中，厚积薄发，在大四的时候，还拿到了执行校长奖学金，排名计算机系前1.5%。在毕业时，她收到了包括杜克大学、南加州大学、帝国理工学院、伦敦大学学院、爱丁堡大学和曼彻斯特大学在内的六所学校抛来的橄榄枝。
“当下很多领域都离不开计算机，也有很多产业寻求人工智能的技术帮助自己转型，掌握计算机会是一项非常实用的技能，也可以拓宽自己未来的选择面。” 也正是因为如此，王彦婷在高考结束后，选择了计算机科学这个专业。

擅长数学和逻辑思维的她，对于编程也有自己的看法。在中学阶段，王彦婷就接触过简单的编程知识，这在她的心中栽下了一颗种子，对她来说，编程就像是在由零和一组成的二进制世界中，构建一个属于自己的小世界。进入宁诺之后，她发现，教授编程语言的课程，很多知识都是互相联会贯通且通过自学和不断练习来掌握的。

在宁诺的计算机科学课程中，同学们可以自行选择自己感兴趣的选修课，在计算机视觉、机器学习、信息可视化、人机交互、人工智能等热门领域进行基础的学习，也有助于同学们申请相应专业的研究生或博士的项目。
在大四的毕业设计中，王彦婷在任剑锋老师的辅导下，着手开始了图像处理的研究。图像取证，就是通过算法来检测图像是否经过篡改来判断图片的真实性。例如说，将一张照片上人像的头部拼接到另一张图片的身体上，从而伪造出一张新的图片。
毕业设计中的自监督模型
这个技术虽然已经诞生多年，但是，目前的算法尚未成熟，王彦婷在项目中着手开始调查现有的算法，并选择利用图像采集时自动记录在图像文件中的EXIF元数据和自监督模型的帮助来检查测试图像的自一致性和完整性。她提到，基于不同数码相机的不同特性，来自不同设备的图像的EXIF数据是不同的。与其他一些基于物理的伪造检测方法不同，它对照片中的内容没有绝对限制，因此可以广泛应用于各种图像中。在此基础上，彦婷尝试预测并更多关注在对结果有积极影响的像素块自比较上，这不仅避免了将不必要的噪声引入结果，还在保证算法准确率的前提下大大提高了算法效率。
用不同方法进行篡改区域定位的一些结果比对
随着计算机的日益普及，越来越多的数字图像可以被接受为教育、商业、法律等领域的授权文件。一些人会利用低门槛的成本和图像处理软件的知识，使篡改过的图像看起来几乎没有篡改痕迹，并借此做一些错误的事情。这使得图像篡改成为一个严重的道德问题，并对社会公义造成了不利的影响。

彦婷指出，这项技术大大减少了区分原始图片和篡改图片的难度，有助于恢复对数字图像的信任，并避免欺诈性图像篡改给社会造成的损失。

在学习上，彦婷是一个非常严谨和有条理的学生，在和老师的沟通交流下，她也逐渐明晰了自己的未来发展方向。哪怕是有一小点疑惑，她都会在老师们的office hour时请教老师，击破一个个疑点难点，并且按照自己的逻辑建立清晰的知识框架。彦婷还记得自己在和老师沟通完，那种豁然开朗的感觉。
王彦婷和她的狗狗乔一
在请教学术问题之余，彦婷也会多和老师们沟通。她说道，“老师们也都是从学生时代这样子一步步走过来的，他们扎根于计算机科学，深耕在不同的细分领域，也给了我许多未来方向选择上的建议。”

王彦婷根据自己的实际情况，最终选择了帝国理工学院Advanced Computing 先进计算硕士研究生项目，深入学习软件开发，也加强数据分析等方面的技能。



宁诺给了我们超长待机的暑假，但同时，它也给了我们丰富的课外活动的选择，让我有机会去学习更多自己感兴趣的知识，也有机会参加更多喜欢的活动。国际化的校园组成让我学会用更开放和包容的眼光去看待这个世界，用辩证的思维去思考问题。最重要的是，宁诺让我意识到个人的无限潜力和力量。

Only when well grounded in Computer Science can Yanting Wang, a graduate of Computer Science in 2020, succeed in securing the further study offer from her dream university. When graduated from UNNC, Yanting received offers from six top universities in the world, including Duke University, University of Southern California, Imperial College, University College London, University of Edinburgh and University of Manchester. She was rewarded the Provost’s Scholarship for her excellent academic performance in the Year 3 (top 1.5% in the school).

She is good at logical thinking and mathematics. Back to the time when she was a high school student, she for the first time learn the computer programming, she found the charisma of programming. She said, programming is building my own little castle in the digital world consists of 0 and 1. After that, she is keen to the computer science and choose it as her undergraduate study.

In the final year project, Yanting Wang started her research on image processing under the guidance of Dr Jianfeng Ren. Image forensics is to detect the authenticity of the image by checking whether the image has been modified. For example, splicing the head of a portrait from one photo onto the body of another, and then creating a new spliced image.

Although this technology has been born for many years, the current algorithm is not yet mature. Yanting did a literature review for this project and choose to uses the information of EXIF metadata—camera specifications that automatically recorded in the file when images are taken—and applying a self-supervised model to check the primitiveness of an image. She mentioned that, based on different features of different digital cameras, the EXIF data is different for images coming from different devices and could be used to check the self-consistency and integrity of the testing image. Unlike some other forgery detection methods such as physics-based method, it does not have limitations on the contents in the photographs, and could thus be applied in a wide range of images. Based on this, Yanting tries to have a reliable prediction on which comparison will be more significant without the ground truth of a splicing image and only do those patch comparisons with the most probability to make positive contributions to the result. This not only avoid introducing noises generated by unnecessary comparisons into the result, but also largely improve the algorithm efficiency.

Due to the increasingly common use of computers, more digital images can be accepted as the authorized documents in the fields such as education, business and law. The low barrier in both cost and knowledge of the image processing software allows some malicious groups to unreasonably take the opportunity of this to make doctored images leaving almost no tampering trace and do something wrong. This has made the image forgery problem to be a serious ethical issue. Yanting said “this technology largely decrease the difficulties in differentiating original and modified contents, and could help return some trust to digital images and help people avoid the losses caused by fraudulent image manipulation.”

Yanting used to organise all the knowledge she learnt from the class and sort out a framework to reinforce it. She would never miss out any minor doubt or uncertainty. In the University of Nottingham Ningbo China, she studied the essential knowledge in computer science. The programme also provides students many optional module to get in touch with detailed disciplines like computer vision, machine learning, information visualization, human computer interaction, artificial intelligence and other hit topics in the moment. Yanting appreciate the learning environment in the UNNC. “We are able to explore our interest through different projects and all the staff in the school are very willing to answer our questions.”

 “UNNC gives us the super long summer vacation (compared with domestic university) and opportunity to participate in the different extra-curriculum activities. The globalised campus makes me inclusive to the big world and also critically view the world. More importantly, I realised that I have the potential to do anything and dare to try. ”

title: 学子故事 | 从涉足多专业，到潜心高端人才咨询，这位读到博后的传播学学姐都经历了啥？
content:
Please Scroll Up for English Version

Liu Dong graduated from UNNC in 2012, with a degree in International Communication and is now serving in Perrett Laver’s London headquarters.
 
Education:
Undergraduate：UNNC, International Communication
Masters: Durham University
PhD: King's College London
Post-doctoral: University of Exeter
 
“It is an extraordinary experience to review my university life from the perspective of a consulting firm after leaving the ivory tower.”

 
Current working situation：
 
I joined Perrett Laver's London headquarters in March last year as a head-hunter. It is a world-class consulting firm specialising in higher education and academic research and shares a close relationship with UNNC, Durham and Exeter. The company is now responsible for the appointment of the next chancellor of King's College London.
 
 
Critical thinking，Inclusive culture，Liberal education
 
Q1: How has your time at UNNC benefited you in your further study and work?
 
UNNC can make you an interesting person and you can meet many fascinating friends. The university offered me chances to adapt to the cultural differences between east and west, making me more tolerant and considerate. My university life here has also gradually improved my language and communication skills, which are also parts of the culture. They together play a significant role later in my PhD and post-doctoral career, as well as in my current job. UNNC also provided me with valuable opportunities to experience the British education model. The gifts UNNC offered us in language and thought will naturally appear later in our lives. As I currently serve in the education industry, which enhances my understating of British education, I can now feel a deeper and stronger resonance with UNNC’s long journey of development and prosperity.

 
Stick to interests，Plan ahead，Explore the unknown
 
Q2:  Do you have any advice for current UNNC students in terms of career development?
 
“Choose the degree that interests you before doing the job that suits you. It is necessary to plan your career goals in advance and hold a definite object in view. Your goal is the greatest inspiration that can lead you to your destination. Try to explore more about the unknown. There are many jobs and chances that you've never thought of or heard of before. After all, ‘Life is like a box of chocolates; you never know what you will get’.”
 
 
Recognise what doesn't interest you
Uninterested work is more painful than no work at all
Enjoying the work process is more important

Q3:  Can you share with us your experience of future planning while studying at UNNC?
 
To be frank, I didn’t have a specific plan for my future career at that time. However, I did recognise what would definitely not attract me. I’ve also found that I’m much more interested in “qualitative research” than “quantitative research”. When I was searching for a suitable job, I always kept what interests me and what does not in mind and interpreted the job requirement very carefully. My suggestion is to let your CV or to be more specific, your interests and experiences, dominate your career choice, instead of revising your CV to cater to the job requirements. Uninterested work is more painful than no work at all. My own experience is that, although it is essential to start a job, it is more important to stick to it and enjoy the entire process.
 
 
Interact more with mentors
Apply your accumulated experience during PhD into Postdoctoral career
Exercise more and keep fit
 
Q4: For many students, it has already been quite exhausting to complete their Postgraduate career, not to mention PhD and Post-doctoral programme. How did you manage to overcome the obstacles you encountered during that process?
 
The biggest challenge was loneliness. It was difficult to separate my life from scientific research. I felt that I could not fully relax as there was no weekend. I desperately wanted to graduate in advance but finally found that it was actually difficult to even graduate on time. As time went on, I did hold the feeling that I could only communicate with my supervisor - there was no one else. I was very lonely and confused about my future career and life expectations during that time. I'm really fortunate to have a considerate and responsible supervisor. Just as the old saying goes, “Being a teacher for only one day entitles one to lifelong respect from the student that befits his father”. Otherwise, it might be impossible for me to walk this challenging path smoothly. Post-doctoral work is actually a research job. I personally think it is not as difficult as the PhD and they are actually very similar. It is very interesting to apply what you have already gained to another related but different project. You can also build your own theory and methodology and make them valuable, which is another fascinating experience. I’ve started to take regular exercise since my second year of PhD and I found it is really important, especially when you feel depressed and stressful. I am trying to get back to my exercise pattern and stick to it. After all, health is the biggest wealth.
 
 
Online teaching has more uncertainties
Multi-campus education can enhance risk resistance
 
Q5: Can you share your views on the current education industry from a professional perspective? For example, whether will be greatly affected by the epidemic and what are the related opportunities and challenges.
 
"The education industry can be divided into many aspects. In theory, online teaching should be an opportunity, but it is also difficult. For example, it is rather impractical to conduct courses that require hands-on activities. Online teaching does have many uncertainties. After a double-blow from Brexit and the current COVID-19 epidemic, British universities are now thoroughly examining their enrolment and financial situation. At this time, the advantages of multiple campuses have gradually appeared as the ability to resist challenges is becoming more important. The regular operation of a university is actually the prerequisite for ensuring the quality of scientific research and teaching. A considerable number of universities are actively proposing schemes to face current challenges. However, due to the uncertainty of this epidemic, many universities can only respond to changes.” 














结语

通过刘冬学姐的经历我们可以发现，UNNC多元而开放的文化环境以及其致力于培养的优秀的批判性思维为她的工作能力奠定了基础。而她对于自身职业兴趣与潜能的不断探索，对于职业规划的前瞻性与平衡生活与工作的能力也值得我们借鉴。希望大家可以从她的转型与尝试中获得启发，做到学以致用，勇敢地走向社会。

title: 理工优秀校友专访｜高阳：从宁诺出发，破茧成蝶，为梦想继续奋斗
content:
高阳，宁波诺丁汉大学理工学院2016届工业设计专业毕业生。毕业后，他入读英国皇家艺术学院和帝国理工学院联培的创新设计工程专业，攻读硕士研究生双学位。目前，他是一名产品设计师，就职于伦敦Seymour Powell产品设计咨询公司。
Yang GAO graduated with a Bachelor of Engineering (BEng) Degree in Product Design and Manufacture (PDM) from University of Nottingham Ningbo China in 2016, and after then he was admitted in Innovation Design Engineering programme offered by Royal College of Art and Imperial College London. Currently, Yang works for Seymour Powell London as a Product Designer.
Please scroll down for more information
高阳
2016届 工业设计
产品设计师
 忆往昔破茧而生

高阳是宁波诺丁汉大学理工学院工业设计专业的第二届学生。整个专业当时初具雏形，作为第二批吃螃蟹的人，高阳表示当初自己的选择成就了现在的他。本科学习期间，他脚踏实地，认真学习专业课程。在孙煦老师的指导建议下，高阳决定出国深造，继续深化认知和技能。

好的开始是成功的一半。“我对设计的兴趣萌发始于UNNC，在这里，我培养了对于设计的热情和最初的认知。后来在工作中接触到的技能大多数都是在研究生阶段得到加强深化。UNNC也拓宽了我的国际视野，为我的研究生申请锦上添花。”

在UNNC毕业后，高阳开启了英国皇家艺术学院和帝国理工学院双学位研究生生涯。两年的学习生活丰富多彩，虽然高阳一路在披襟斩棘，升级打怪，但收获的是沉甸甸的知识，并结识了许多志同道合的朋友。“研究生毕业后我尝试过创业，但后来体会到创业不易。一是自身阅历不够，二是发现我真正的兴趣是通过设计服务接触不同的项目，所以决定努力进入心仪的公司，积累经验。”

念今朝厚积薄发

目前，高阳是一名产品设计师，就职于伦敦Seymour Powell。工作职责是通过对客户需求进行创造性分析，结合设计思维和技巧，完成在未来一定时间内具有商业价值的产品设计。“我喜欢这份工作，除了设计思维本身给我带来的兴奋感和因项目不断学习的新鲜感，更重要的是在为客户解决目标用户所面临的问题后，我的社会责任感得以满足所带来的喜悦。”

对于高阳来说，虽然少数时候设计的纯粹性可能受到其商业环境的限制，但这反而成为他不断前进的动力之一，锻炼了他的专业能力。很多国际知名设计都是能很好的平衡设计与商业性，并做到两全其美的。

成功向来不是一蹴而就的，产品设计这一行业比较遵循常规发展路线，积累扎实经验并稳步提升。谈到个人成就时，高阳谦虚地回应道谈自己的“成就”还为时过早。不过在看到自身投入心血的项目陆续进入实施阶段，的确是会很有成就感。

高阳表示，“如果想要胜任这份工作，至少得具有相关专业的本科学历背景，但重点还是需要看个人所具备的设计思维和技巧。在这个职位上，如果想获得成功必须持有开放包容的心态以及具备为用户解决问题的责任感。积极的团队合作能力也不可或缺。”而这些技能，他在宁诺的学习过程中早就深有体会。

目前在英国工作的高阳，对于文化差异和东西方思维逻辑不同也有了更深的认识。在国际化的职业环境下，文化多样性是必不可少的，多元的文化背景也有利于减少偏见的存在。同时，也需要每一位员工可以做到换位思考，更全面的理解不同文化之间的可贵之处。在研究生期间，高阳是班级里为数不多的中国学生。每一次做小组项目时，老师都会将他们安排进不同的小组，鼓励学生充分交流不同的文化，这一点，也促进了他对于西方文化的吸收与理解。
畅未来寄语UNNCers
“UNNC这四年塑造了我的人生观和价值观，也让我对未来的职场规划有了清晰的认识。这四年里，虽然有挫折有风雨，但这些都是我成长的催化剂。“

高阳鼓励学弟学妹在假期多做一些实习项目，积累行业经验。如果有读研意向，可以提早着手规划。国外研究生经历为他留在英国工作打下良好的基础。但是国外行业内竞争激烈，高阳建议可以在领英多找些前辈约coffee talk交流想法。“祝愿学弟学妹珍惜在UNNC的学习时光，享受其中，找到内心所爱，并情愿为之奋斗。如果有需要，欢迎通过微信交流想法。”
When Yang GAO joined Product Design and Manufacture (PDM) programme, he was the second cohort of it. Although at that time, they could hardly find much experience to learn from his senior students, he would very much like to share his experience with his fellow students.

Studying at UNNC broadens his international view and brings him the authentic British education system. In the UNNC, for the first time he got to know the concept of design and lighted his passion to it. He felt grateful that he chose PDM and received many advice from his teachers.

Therefore, after graduating from UNNC, Yang GAO successfully started his double-master study at Royal College of Art and Imperial College London, through which both art and engineering knowledge was enhanced and fulfilled. The course invited the professionals from both sides to pass on the latest design trends and technology information, encourage students to think about the sustainable concepts with decades forecast. During this period, he further enhanced the all design skills and also he met some friends from different culture who he truly respected and shared the common interests with, which for him was as much precious as the course itself is.

Currently, Yang works for Seymour Powell as a Product Designer. The responsibility of this role covers broad aspects, which for short is to create the design with a certain level of business value through logically analysing client’s requirements and creatively applying design thinking.
 
“Working as a designer is definitely delightful. The joy comes from many aspects, such as design thinking itself, consistent-learning mindset and problem-solving process. Although in few cases the design concept may be constrained by its business environment, it is definitely a positive challenge for designers to polish design ability. There are countless design cases well balancing these two parts, which becomes classics through history.” Yang enjoys his current work even the challenges of it.
 
He said that the product design industry follows the standard route, which people start with internship or entry level position, then gradually reach higher levels based on their accomplishment. When it comes to his accomplishment, Yang said that it’s still too early to talk about it, but he did feel a sense of achievement when he finished the projects precisely and looked forward to their production.
 
He mentioned that four skills are very important to success in this industry, which is keeping an open attitude, taking responsibility, being passionate about design as well as working seamlessly with team members. “The minimal requirement would be having a related education experience and degree, such as a Degree of Art and Engineering. For most of cases it really depends on the strategic design ability and skills the person has.”

In addition, he mentioned the skills of transcultural communication is vital to his current working environment. His co-workers come from different countries and cultural background. The diversity helps to avoid bias and minimise the risks. Different cultural background and logic of thinking may also cause barriers of communication. Therefore, to overcome it, he always keeps an open mind and be inclusive to different culture. 
 
Wishes to UNNCers
“It’s been a joy to study at UNNC. The four years study had a positive influence on my values, principals and rules. I believe that nothing is impossible so that I can achieve my goals with a strong attitude. Throughout the journey in UNNC, it’s not always smooth but luckily every single experience has contributed to push me forward. “
 
Yang GAO encourages the current PDM students to improve themselves through some internships. The replacement during student period is also an option. If students are interested in some specific companies, make sure to have a list of their required skills and start to prepare on an early stage. If some students are considering about the global positions, a master study could be a transition. Students can understand the local culture and therefore re-estimate their decisions through it. A coffee talk with professionals in the industry could be very beneficial. He wishes all UNNCers to enjoy their study life and hopefully they all can find their passions.

title: 学生故事 | 张文欣 · 但知前路，不畏路远
content:
张文欣
16 级国际经济与贸易专业
牛津大学、剑桥大学双 offer
国家留学基金委奖学金
2018 年、2019 年浙江省奖学金
2019 年 President’s Scholarship & Best Student of the Year
2020 年浙江省优秀毕业生
2020 年校长推荐优秀毕业生奖


1

  从迷茫到认定  

和其他人一样，在最开始面对琳琅满目的不同专业时，张文欣也曾经感到过难以抉择：“我当初选择 IET 的时候对它并没有什么概念，但到了大二，发现 IET 其实会从两个方面帮助我们提升自己。一方面是知识的沉淀，让你具有国际视野，更加关注时事热点，以及在面对数据时保持“独立”，拥有自己的想法。而另一方面，是一种软技能的提升——主动思考和逻辑化思维。”

一个主动思考并且很有条理的人，认定了一个目标就会不断前行——张文欣正是这样的一个女孩。在宁诺的四年学习生活中，她一直坚定不移的向着自己的目标冲刺，并且在毕业季最终来临的时候为自己交出了一份满意的答卷。


当然，在上下求索的道路上也会遇到纷至沓来的学术难题，张文欣也慢慢总结出了自己独特的方法用来克服学术上的困难：“

我觉得首先是要去不断的总结反思，每隔一周或一个月，根据自己上课的笔记，总结一遍并列好框架，做好思维导图，方便期末复习；在按照章节复习时，其实可以根据自己的逻辑来调整老师所给 PPT的顺序，顺应自己的思维，对应自己的理解，这样更容易抓到知识的重点。


最后一点就是如何用搜索引擎寻找题目的答案。我平时不会直接搜寻完整的题目，而是会选择先去查找关键词的含义，进一步去了解题目的相关背景，这些是你思考一道问题的基础。然后再根据你已知的信息和这些附加信息，去尝试是否能自己独立推理出结果。这样其实也能起到锻炼思维的作用。”


张文欣说，其实学习的方法有很多，最重要的是找到适合自己的。



2
  第二课堂与实践  

大一的时候张文欣通过面试加入了社团中心和 SPDPO，在一年的干事生涯中她学会了更好的在学习与组织中找到自己的“平衡点”，如何在多项任务的压力下仍能保持高效运转。在这期间，她也参与到了很多的大型活动的策划中，在项目背后辛勤工作。她说：“当全程参与一个项目时，从项目启动再到项目落地，结束的那一刻真的很有成就感。”


张文欣还特别提到她通过 NAA（诺丁汉卓越奖）参加过的“格莱珉银行咨询项目”。“NAA 对我们有很多帮助，比如会有机会参加一些咨询项目，也可以在就业办的活动中学到很多职场干货，还有的项目会要求我们在平时看一些阅读材料，每周要定量形成一篇总结，这不仅能够提高我的阅读与写作能力，同时也在每周的积累中学到了很多额外知识。我觉得这些软性加硬性的‘福利’，是 NAA 能够带给每个人最大的财富。

其实学校经常能够提供一些帮助大家提升的活动机会，希望大家能好好把握。”



3
  付出才会获得机遇  

张文欣说，在学校组织社团的工作其实是为了为以后的实习提前作准备。

在假期生活中，她在一家资信评级机构当实习分析师。起初，张文欣做着和其他实习生一样的工作，填写资料、整理底稿。后来她的组长将撰写一篇主体与相关债项跟踪报告的任务交给她，收到任务的时候，激动的同时也伴随了巨大的压力——她之前没有接触过这类报告更别说写报告了。

随后，她去翻阅了多份报告、以最短的时间掌握报告的框架逻辑，思考各板块撰写细节，独立与对方公司负责人沟通，最终功夫不负有心人，她高效将一篇完整且高质量的报告交给了组长，并且获得了组长的赞许。也正是这一份报告让组长看到了她的认真负责和能力，组长愿意将另一份报告交给她完成并由她独立撰写。


张文欣还建议千万别“水”实习，也许一开始的工作很琐碎，让你觉得是没有意义的，但当你能够把简单、重复的事情一丝不苟的做好，让大家看到你的价值后，你一定会得到重用的。只有自己重视实习的工作，别人才会愿意给你一个提升自己的机会，让你去做一些更有挑战、更为核心的任务。也只有这样，当你之后在写简历的时候才能真情实感，才能有干货的输出。纸上谈兵一般去过度包装自己简历上的实习经历是很空洞且不真实的。

这一次的实习让张文欣很感动，同时也收获了很多的自信：组长用自己的时间给她解答疑问，最后的成果得到其他人的赞赏与肯定…这些都是她自己争取到的。保持谦卑，主动学习，不放弃任何一个机会，自己才会收获和成长更多。



4
  奖学金对于自己的意义  

张文欣说，收到今年校长推荐优秀毕业生奖邮件的那一刻，惊讶与喜悦并存。“这份奖学金是给自己的一种肯定，也是一份证明，证明努力真的能被看见。大学四年，从前 20% 到 10% 最后到 1% 再到牛津剑桥，真的付出了很多。但幸运的是，最终结果是好的，是值得的。我会将这份证明化作成一种激励，在我将来走向分析师的道路上想要停一停时，它能让我重拾信心，继续走的更远、更坚定。”


采访的最后，张文欣说道：“大学生活远不只有学术本身，更重要的是从学术中获得了什么。永远保持思辩精神、开放包容的态度、志同道合的朋友以及坚定不移追求自己所热爱的。这些都将是伴随你一生的财富。感恩宁诺提供了这样一个平台让我成长为了更好的自己。我将永远铭记杨福家校长的毕业寄语 「做人第一 修业第二」。在未来的旅途中，存在于我头脑和心中的火种永不熄灭。”





拿到双 Offer 的张文欣即将前往剑桥，开启自己的求学生涯。我们也希望，在今后的日子里，她能够继续秉承自己的信念，坚定不移的在自己选择的道路上走下去。

title: 我的大学 | 李钧泽：在这里走过的每一步都有意义
content:
Li Junze is a recent graduate of the International Business Economics programme at the University of Nottingham Ningbo China (UNNC). From disorientation in the beginning to his current confidence, he is now ready to pursue further study at the London School of Economics and Political Science. In this interview, Junze recalled his student days, and shared some of his experiences, allowing us to follow his path in retrospect to explore his experience at UNNC.

Please scroll down for the full English version.
李钧泽
Li Junze
毕业年份：2020年
就读专业：国际商务经济学
毕业去向：伦敦政治经济学院
毕业高中：山东省莱州一中

Interview with Li Junze 李钧泽采访视频

“很留恋这里”
“很留恋这里！”在毕业过后的采访中，李钧泽用最直白的话语表达了他对宁波诺丁汉大学的留恋。“四年很美好，转瞬即逝”，即将前往伦敦继续深造的他，回忆起自己在宁诺的学习生涯，从初入宁诺的短暂迷茫，到如今走出宁诺的自信从容；从聆听学长学姐们的分享，到帮助学弟学妹们发展自我；从和朋友们相识相交，到如今各奔前程。这段学习经历不仅使他扩展了知识的广度，同时也帮助他开掘了思想的深度。在本次采访中，李钧泽在回忆自己的学习生涯的同时，也分享了他所总结的一些经验，让我们跟随他记忆的脚步，探寻他在宁诺的经历与成长。


雏鹰起飞前的换羽期
在高三的一场饭局之中，李钧泽第一次了解到中外合办大学。高考结束后，李钧泽和父母一起对国内的中外合办大学进行了详细的了解和分析。最终，李钧泽认为最适合他的大学是宁波诺丁汉大学，并选择了这所学校。“学校提供了非常好的平台，资源丰富，有益于学生未来的发展，但最重要的还是我们如何去利用好这个平台。” 而合理利用学校的资源与优势，正是李钧泽所擅长的。


在观察中学习，在交流中成长
在问及如何确定自己的目标时，李钧泽讲述了他的经历。在iWeek（新生适应周）期间以及参与的社团活动中，李钧泽结识了许多乐于分享的学长学姐。“一开始进来（宁诺）的感觉，像是个温馨的大家庭，每个人都乐意去分享经验、帮助他人。”  李钧泽这么形容宁诺的氛围。通过与学长学姐的交流和自己的观察，李钧泽找到了学习参考的对象，并通过实践将他人的经历改造成适合自我的全新规划。“无论是大一的暑假还是其他时候，每一个阶段都能找到学习的对象。”后来，李钧泽也将学长学姐们带给他的这份温暖与力量延续了下去，成为学长、朋辈导师的他，经常为学弟学妹们解疑答惑、分享学术经验，被大家笑称为“多老师”。
对于出国交换，李钧泽也有他自己的见解。他认为出国交换最大的收获并不仅仅是在专业课程中所学到的知识，而是了解当地文化并与其交流后所带来的国际化视野的提升。“我在英国旅行的过程中了解到英格兰人和苏格兰人的差异，个人认为苏格兰人比较粗犷一些，英格兰人更绅士一些”，李钧泽以他在英国的旅行见闻举例，“其实我很期待有机会去到不同的国家和地区，这些经历对你以后无论是工作还是思维的开阔都非常重要”。同时他也表示，积极交流是商学院课程学习的一个十分重要的途径，无论是与老师还是和同学交流，思维的碰撞都能带来不一样的东西。

商学院之外的另一个课堂
在商学院的学习之外，李钧泽还从另一个课堂中学到了许多。在他口中，参加社团活动和广交朋友都给他带来了许多成长，充实了他的大学生活。大二学年在商英社做过负责人的他，在谈及社团带给他的益处时，说道：“我觉得社团主要带给我了两点，首先是学术之外的团队协作的经历，第二点就是结识了很多有共同兴趣的朋友。”而大学认识的志同道合的朋友对李钧泽来说是不可或缺的重要部分，无论是从生活还是从学业来说，朋友都给他带来了很多帮助，让他的大学生涯更加丰富多彩。
在参与社团活动和与朋友交往的过程中，如何平衡这些与学习之间的关系是一个不可避免的问题。李钧泽认为，这个问题实质上是如何在生活和学习中实现平衡。“无法完全平衡，没有绝对标准。”他是这么回答的。他认为，生活和学习是相互交织在一起的，无法完全以时间为标准区分开来，如果强行区分开反而可能使事情更加杂乱，效率降低。我认为自己比较有效的做法是放平心态，随机应变，见招拆招，保持生活和学习的动态平衡。

“静下心沉淀自己，寻找未来的方向”
在采访的末尾，当被问及有什么和学弟学妹们分享的话时，李钧泽给出了他的见解。他先讲述了他自己这一年来的体验，“过得十分匆忙，让自己有些找不到节奏和方向”。大四秋季学期一连串的考试、申研、写论文，还有春季学期突发的疫情导致李钧泽在这一年里的时间十分紧凑。如今毕业之后，他终于找到时间去沉静自己的心，反思总结过去的一年。他认为，这样做可以更好地沉淀自己，从过去的成功与失败中收获经验，并明确未来的前进方向，使自己不迷茫，而这种状态便是他所追求的新常态。“希望学弟学妹们在面对困难时能够保持坚韧与勇敢，在前进的道路上也不忘时常放慢脚步，沉淀反思自己，人生没有无用的经历，让每一步都走得有意义。”

未来的道路
“毕业之后还是先继续读书吧。” 当谈到对未来职业规划的时候，他透露了自己所规划的两条截然不同的道路。第一个方向是在读完研究生后步入职场，从事项目管理或者管理咨询的工作，然后通过继续读MBA来丰富自己的知识。第二个方向是在读完研究生后继续攻读博士，在学术研究领域继续深入，然后回到学校当一名教授。他有着明确的方向，但世间风云变幻，随机应变是他的态度，他会在每个路口再抉择，踏实走好脚下的每一步，就好！
My UNNC Story
Li Junze: Every step I take here is meaningful!
"I’ll miss this place very much!" expressed Li Junze during this interview after graduation. He used the most understandable words to describe UNNC’s profound presence in his memories. "The four years were wonderful but fleeting," said Junze, as he recalled his journey at UNNC. From disorientation in the beginning to his current confidence, he is now ready to pursue further study at the London School of Economics and Political Science. From listening to seniors sharing their experience, to eventually helping other fellow students, from building friendships to parting ways, Junze reflected on how his educational journey broadened his knowledge and deepened his insights. In this interview, Junze recalled his student days, and shared some of his experiences, allowing us to follow his path in retrospect to explore his experience at UNNC.
 Slide up for more details.
 Ready to rise and take off
At a dinner during his senior year at high school, Li Junze first learned about Sino-foreign universities. After the Gaokao, Junze and his parents together explored this type of university thoroughly. Junze eventually found that UNNC matched his ideal requirements, and he decided to attend university here. "UNNC provides a great platform that is rich in resources, which can benefit students' future development, and students need to consider how to take advantage of them." Junze is especially adept at appropriately taking advantage of UNNC’s strengths.

However, Junze’s journey at UNNC was not all smooth sailing. "When I first entered the university, I struggled a lot, and even thought of dropping out to repeat another year and then enter a traditional university." Consequently, Junze was facing below-average grades by the spring of his freshman year. Nevertheless, through his parents’ support and senior students’ encouragement, Junze adjusted his mindset and changed himself during the autumn semester. He then quickly caught up with the university’s academic pace and actively began to participate in university events. As Junze discussed this period, he highlighted how grateful he was for his parents’ selfless giving and support. "My parents paid a lot of attention to my behaviour, like whether their son from a small town could adjust to a new environment or whether there would be a recognition gap between other students and me. However, they provided full support because they hoped I could use the opportunity to open the door to a bigger world."

Learning from observation, growing from communication
When asked about how he targeted his goals, Li Junze explained how his experience during iWeek (new students' induction week) and with student organisations was formative because he connected with and learned from many senior students. When describing UNNC’s community, Junze said, "Upon entering, one can feel that UNNC is like a warm family, and everyone is happy to share." Through communicating with senior students and through observation, Junze found role models worth referencing and adapted other role models’ experiences to form his ideal plan. "No matter the period, everyone can find a role model for different stages in life."

With regard to studying abroad, Junze also gave his opinions. He thinks that the most significant value in studying abroad does not lie solely in the knowledge learned from courses, but in gaining an elevated international view from communicating with a different culture." I learned during my UK trip the contrast between the English and the Scottish." Junze used this example to explain the following, "I look forward to travelling to different countries because it can critically influence our future profession or other experiences." At the same time, Junze also pointed out that communication is essential in NUBS China’s courses because interpersonal communication with professors or peers can stimulate different ideas and thoughts.

Classroom outside of NUBS China
Aside from studying at NUBS China, Junze also learned a lot from other places. He gained many benefits from clubs and friendships, which enriched his university life. During his second year, he became the leader of the Sunny-Biz Student Society. As Junze discussed the ways he benefited from the club, he explained, "I think the club gifted me two things — teamwork experience, and friendship built through the experience." Friends who share common bonds are vital to Junze. In both daily and academic life, friends gave him support and enlivened his UNNC journey.

When actively attending clubs and maintaining friendships, the balance between such involvement and learning becomes an inevitable issue. Junze believes that the problem lies in balancing social and academic life. "It is impossible to achieve total balance, and there is no absolute standard," said Junze when he responded to the issue. He thinks that daily life and study time are intertwined, meaning that they cannot be easily split into different periods. If one tries to forcefully split them apart, one may face more struggles and lower efficiency. The best way might be to appropriately position one’s attitude and mindset, be flexible with changes, adapt to emerging issues, and achieve a balance between the dynamic pace of daily life and studying.

Space and calm to explore future paths
As the interview came to an end, Junze shared his thoughts when asked about what he wanted to share with younger students. He first described his experience during the past year, "I was swamped, to the point where I could not find a clear direction." Final year examinations, graduate school applications, papers, and the recent COVID-19 pandemic made Junze’s schedule in the past year very packed. Since graduation, he has finally found some time to be calm and reflect on the previous year. He believes that by doing so, he can better position himself, digest recent accomplishments, and clarify his future direction to prevent himself from feeling lost. Such a state of mind is something he looks for in daily life.

Future paths
"I will first be continuing my studies after graduation." Junze mentioned his graduate school choice as he talked about his future path. While conversing over career development, Junze revealed two different paths he planned for himself. The first plan is to enter a company to gain project management experience after graduating with a master’s degree, and then later pursue an MBA programme. The second plan is to pursue a PhD degree after a master’s programme, to delve deeper into academia and return to university to become an academic staff. No matter which choice, Junze gradually equips the ability to cherish the moment and keep his wits about his future.

title: 我的大学⎮乔虹玮、王一慧：“姐妹花”在宁诺勇敢蜕变
content:
Qiao Hongwei and Wang Yihui, recent graduates of Finance, Accounting and Management programme, recalled their four years in the University of Nottingham Ningbo China (UNNC) together and unanimously stated that "transformation" was the strongest benefit they gained here. The opportunities and challenges given by UNNC have changed many of the two ladies' choices both in their personalities and learning experiences. Let us listen to their stories.

Please scroll down for the English version.

乔虹玮 Qiao Hongwei
毕业年份：2020年
就读专业：金融财务与管理
毕业高中：浙江镇海中学
毕业去向：伦敦帝国理工学院

王一慧 Wang Yihui
毕业年份：2020年
就读专业：金融财务与管理
毕业高中：宁波效实中学
毕业去向：伦敦帝国理工学院

双双被帝国理工录取的好姐妹乔虹玮和王一慧回忆起大学四年，一致表示“蜕变”是她们在宁诺描绘的最浓烈的底色。不论是个性还是学习生活，宁诺这样一个国际化的平台赋予她们的机遇和挑战都改变了两个女孩的许多选择，为她们的人生带来浓墨重彩的一页。

大学的他们也拿了不少奖学金，他们没有浪费，反而有了理财的意识。“大学四年中，我们拿到的奖学金累计有十万元，我们已经拿了一部分用作理财投资，剩下的会用来带父母去完成毕业旅行。”

Interview with Qiao Hongwei & Wang Yihui
乔虹玮与王一慧视频采访

01
“不是每个人一开始就闪闪发光”
“蜕变带给我力量。”乔虹玮认为自己四年最大的改变是在性格上，“我之前是一个有点内向的人，但是从大一开始，宁诺校内的CELE（Centre for English Language Education）英语语言教学中心老师们都不断在课堂上鼓励我们勇敢表达自己，加上周围小伙伴们的影响，我变得越来越开朗，越来越自信。

王一慧也谈到：“之前我在高中不是非常活泼的人，初入大学时给他人的印象也是“安静的学霸”，不太愿意表达自己。当时大一上写作课，考试结束后CELE的老师给每人写了封信，给我的那封信里写到‘希望在课堂上听见我更多的声音’，从那以后，我就开始注意更勇敢地表达自己。大一下学期的group discussion（小组讨论）中，我主动担任了协调者的角色，取得了很好的成绩，让我进一步更加肯定了老师对我的期许。”
正是有了这段受到老师引导下的改变，王一慧的大二更加顺风顺水：之前抗拒的office hour（面对面答疑）变得更加有吸引力；认识了许多好朋友，学会作为倾听者和观察者，观察他们如何和老师沟通， “虽然老师们上课都会无私地讲授很多，但是私下交流时会迸发更多的insights（深度见解），这让我们对于知识点的理解更加深入。”

除此之外，两人借助宁诺提供的国际化平台继续寻求改变：乔虹玮曾担任于宁波举办的第三届中东欧国家教育项目洽谈会志愿者、宁波市第一届模拟联合国大赛志愿者，并赴挪威参加夏校课程；王一慧则参加了校内组织AIESEC举办的“你好，生命”和“SunShine”活动，前者在温州帮助野生动物保护组织宣传动物保护和领养知识，后者在俄罗斯叶卡捷琳堡开展英语教学和中国文化的教育工作。

02
双双被录取的秘密：
寻找自身经历和梦校课程的契合点
谈到为何被帝国理工录取，王一慧认为非常重要的一点是通过头脑风暴、不断寻找自己的经历和心仪学校课程的契合点，不断挖掘并体现在文书里面，这样能够吸引他们，感受到学生对他们的喜爱；同时通过短期、长期的职业规划，展现自己对未来的清晰思考。

乔虹玮的规划离不开商学院搭建的平台。大二时，她参加了商学院的NAA（Nottingham Advantage Award）诺丁汉卓越奖商业咨询项目，由宁诺商学院老师带领，对接真实的企业，构思咨询报告，“通过一系列的学习，我掌握了咨询行业部分业界思维模式以及分析方法。”王一慧的规划同样与在商院的收获密不可分，她担任过商学院的研究助理，研究“社会环境对中国消费者手机品牌选择的影响”。这个经历不仅让她收获了市场调研和数据分析的能力，也让她进一步明确了自己对于消费行业的探索欲，为她之后在职场中做出细分行业的选择指明了方向。

她们也十分感谢商学院的老师们：“他们中的很多人已经取得了一定的成就，但他们在课堂上总能够循循善诱，引导还是'小白'的我们，课后也总是不厌其烦地解答我们的问题。这让我们浸润在知识中的同时，也总是被温暖沐浴着。” 由于出色的成绩和丰富的社会实践经历，两人均获得了多个奖学金，其中有国家奖学金，浙江省政府奖学金和宁诺的校长奖学金，后者在商学院仅有1%的名额。被问及奖学金利用率时，王一慧和乔虹玮表示，大学四年下来累计有将近十万的金额，她们作为商科生，选择拿一部分出来，加之所学知识的运用，尝试理财、投资等，比如学着分析外币的汇率走势，选择合适的时机运用远期合同等衍生品买卖英镑，为即将到来的留学生活做打算；同时想攒下一部分金额，毕业时带父母出去旅行，感念家人对自己的无私支持。学会回馈，是一种能力，也是一种品德。

03
学习秘籍：
音乐和体育加持，善问与规划并行
乔虹玮的特长有长笛和电子琴，她喜欢音乐带来的感官体验，也热爱通过音乐认识伙伴、提升自信、获得力量。王一慧也喜欢音乐，“音乐就像生活，缓急轻重都是节奏的表现。把握自己的节奏，就是把握生活的秘密。”同时，体育运动爱好者王一慧说：“运动分泌的多巴胺能带给我们清爽愉悦的体验，这也是放松方式的一种，就像中场休息，预备接下来的发力。”

关于学术成绩，乔虹玮认为，要珍惜老师们office hour的机会，多去多问，养成习惯。“我喜欢早早地赶到lecture（讲座）教室，选一个能近距离和老师沟通的位置，利用课后课间询问，不仅可以聊到本堂课的内容精髓，同时可能会拓宽到整个课程的逻辑框架，甚至是其他的有关个人规划的深远建议。”王一慧也同意这样的观点，“最初我也不怎么和老师交流，但经历了转变后，开始敢于讲出自己内心的想法，而不再总是一个人消化。其实，学会提问也是一个技能。”
除了多和老师交流，课前预习、课后整理，组建学习小组进行笔记分享、分工整理阅读材料，也是她们的秘诀。“尤其是time writing（限时写作）的课程，我们会约几个小伙伴一起讨论主题和需要的材料，互相交流获得灵感的碰撞。”

时间管理上，两人表示，一定要尽早规划属于自己的“时间线”，大三开始着手准备浏览各个心仪学校的硬性软性条件，比如GPA和项目等，并针对性地制定策略。大四时，乔虹玮平时进行扎实的时间管理，专心学术；每个周末专门留出一整天准备申请事项。“比如语言考试，由于宁诺是全英文教学，大一也进行了和雅思题型十分类似的学术写作和口语训练，所以不需要花费大量时间准备，而是把时间放在更需要的地方。”

04
不留遗憾，学会取舍
谈起四年的收获和遗憾，乔虹玮感慨没能参加更多的社团组织，通过社团积累下深厚的友谊。“开始时，我以学术为主，回头看发现体验也很重要，还是有得必有失吧。”关于做出选择，乔虹玮提出要根据实际情况、衡量得失，并拿考证举例：“我考了高级商业会计师证书，虽然帮助了某些课程的学习，也打下了更扎实的专业基础，但如果再给我一次选择，我会把考证的时间拿来做更多有趣且有意义的事。“

王一慧则提出鼓励大家放手去做，“我的一些选择还是略为保守，如果再给我一次机会，我会更加大胆。”她认为，某些时候需要做一个risk taker（风险承担者），不能只做百分之百有把握的事情，那样会被禁锢在自己设定的条条框框里。不给自己的潜力设限。勇敢地去冲击更好的，才能够不留遗憾。

两人同时肯定：在不同阶段学会多样化试错，不要盯着一个不放，这种避开其他路径的方式是不可取的。虽然每个人对于自己的未来有了初步的规划，但每个阶段的重点不同，空间也无限大，要勇于尝试、获得属于自己的蜕变。

祝福送给这对姐妹，希望她们能在追梦路上越走越远！


My UNNC Story ⎮ Qiao Hongwei and Wang Yihui: Transformation and growing  together 

Qiao Hongwei and Wang Yihui, both admitted into Imperial College, recalled their four years in the University of Nottingham Ningbo China (UNNC) together and unanimously stated that "transformation" was the most substantial benefit they gained here. The opportunities and challenges given by UNNC have changed many of the two girl’s choices, both in their personalities and learning experiences. Let us listen to their stories.

Slide up for more details.
 Transformation brings power
Recalling four years at UNNC, Hongwei believes that her most significant change has been in character. "I was a somewhat an introverted person before, but from the beginning of my freshman year, the tutors from CELE (Centre for English Language Education) in UNNC constantly encouraged us to express ourselves in class." Yihui recalled the encouragement from her tutor who wrote everyone a letter after their examinations. The letter to her conveyed the message that she should express herself more in class. Since then, Yihui’s voice has begun to become braver. This transformation under the guidance of their teachers eased their second year. They met many good friends and learned to become better listeners and observers.

Imperial College’s admission: Matching UNNC’s courses with experience
When discussing the reasons why Imperial College accepted them, Yihui believes that through brainstorming, it is essential to connect personal experience with your favourite course. You need to continually unearth and reflect on these connections in the application so that they grab the attention of the admission officers, making them feel the student’s inclinations. 


Through the platform provided by UNNC, they gained a variety of international experience, which greatly enhanced their practical awareness. Hongwei was a volunteer in the third Central and Eastern European Countries Education Project Fair and in the first round of the Model United Nations Competition in Ningbo. She also went to Norway to participate in a summer school course and gained tuition fee waivers. Yihui participated in the "Hello, Life" and "SunShine" activities organised by the organisation AIESEC on campus. The former project promoted animal rescue and wildlife protection in Wenzhou, while the latter was teaching English and Chinese culture in Yekaterinburg, Russia.

Outstanding academic performance comes from scientific methods.
Due to their outstanding achievements and rich experience in social work, both students received multiple scholarships, including the Zhejiang Provincial Scholarship and the President Scholarship. The latter is only given to students whose performance is in the top 1% of the business school. When asked about how the scholarships were used, they said that they had both accumulated nearly 100,000RMB each in the past four years. As business students, they used some of it for financial investment and some of it was saved to take their parents travelling after graduating.

Hongwei believes that we should cherish the opportunities offered by office hours to ask more questions and develop better habits. She likes to rush to the lecture room early and choose a seat that has the best view and is convenient for communication with the teacher. During office hours, a conversation helps you to not only understand the key ideas of the class but also provides much further insights into the entire course. Yihui also agreed with this view, “I didn’t communicate much with the teachers at first, but after undergoing some change, I decided to put my head above the parapet and began to speak out my thoughts. In fact, learning to ask questions is a vital skill."

In addition to communicating with teachers, they also gave useful advice on preparing and reviewing classes, organising study groups to share notes and sorting out reading materials. In terms of time management, they planned their own "timeline" as early as possible.

In the final year, Hongwei used solid time management to concentrate on studies and on the weekends, she set aside an hour to prepare her postgraduate applications. 

Apart from their outstanding academic performance, they also kept their passion for music and sports. Hongwei loves playing the flute and electronic organ, enjoying the sensory experience brought on by music. Yihui also likes music, "Music is the expression of rhythm. Maintaining your own rhythm is the secret of life." At the same time, both of them are sports enthusiasts. Yihui said, "Sports raise your dopamine levels and that can refresh and relax you, which is just like an intermission before preparing for your next effort."

Gains and thoughts
With regard to making choices, Hongwei suggested that gauging situations through a cost-benefit mindset is useful. Yihui encourages her younger peers to try things out without having regrets, "Some of my choices were slightly conservative. If you gave me another chance, I would be bolder." She believes that sometimes you ought to be a risk-taker, and you can’t do things with 100% certainty all the time.
They also affirmed that it is important to diversify your focus at different stages and not be limited by given standards. Although everyone has a preliminary plan for their own future, the focus of each stage is different and the space for opportunity is vast. You should be brave enough to try and transform yourself.
