主题示范课程
01
第五代移动通信
--现实还是口号？
13:15-14:00
迪林勋爵楼 A05
第五代移动通信（5G）可以将数十亿用户通过终端设备（如智能家电、联网汽车、智能手机、笔记本电脑等）相互连接，实现“超连接社会”。基于高速率、低功耗、低延时和高连接密度的特点，5G可为用户提升三大业务服务：3D/超高清视频等大流量移动宽带业务，大规模物联网业务，以及如无人驾驶、工业自动化等需要低时延、高可靠连接的业务。

本堂示范课将介绍5G时代的核心技术，并与其前身（3G-UMTS，4G-LTE-Pro）进行比较。关博士还将带大家讨论5G技术在交通、医疗、娱乐和工业自动化等领域的潜力。

主讲人: 关秋峰 博士

关秋峰博士现任宁诺电气与电子工程系助理教授。在2016年加入宁诺之前，关博士已经拥有15年的电信工程教学与研究经验。他的研究兴趣包括异构网络、LTE和5G的移动性管理技术，并在该领域的期刊和会议上发表了一系列的出版物。他目前还是宁诺理工学院的招生与国际关系主任和人工智能与优化研究团队的成员。
 
关博士是美国电气与电子工程师协会（IEEE）和英国工程技术学会（IET）的活跃成员。他曾在2008-2010年期间担任IET马来西亚青年专家组主席，并在2011年至2014年被任命为英国IET委员会成员。他还是IET的国际专业注册顾问（IPRA）以及IET专业资格审查面试官（PRI），代表IET面试特许工程师候选人。

02
媒体素养和数字素养
14:10-15:00
迪林勋爵楼 A04
媒体素养是正确认识和使用媒介的一种能力，这种能力是公民了解、使用、判断媒介以及媒介信息的能力，具有媒体素养的人能更加意识到媒体对人们信念、态度、价值观、行为和政治的影响。

数字素养是在数字环境下利用信息技术手段和方法，快速有效地发现、获取、评价、整合、交流信息的综合技能与文化素养。

本堂示范课上，Gilardi博士将对媒体素养和数字素养进行介绍，展示两者之间的异同。他还将带大家探讨关于媒体消费者和生产者的问题。

主讲人: Filippo Gilardi 博士
Gilardi博士是宁诺人文与社会科学学院国际传播系的系主任，同时担任宁诺亚太研究院副主任。他的研究领域集中在媒体融合、版权保护和全球数字平台的发展。

Gilardi博士是英国高等教育学院的首席研究员，也是英国皇家艺术学会的研究员。

03
凯恩斯在上个世纪提出的通论，
现在仍然适用吗？
15:10-16:00
迪林勋爵楼 A04
约翰·梅纳德·凯恩斯（John Maynard Keynes）在1936年发表了他在宏观经济理论方面最具启发性的杰作：《就业、利息和货币通论》，抨击了全球经济萧条时期盛行的古典宏观经济正统理论。

在本节示范课程中，Scheffel博士将简要总结凯恩斯在《通论》中提出的主要论点，并讨论其与当今全球经济形势的相关性。

主讲人:Eric Michael Scheffel 博士
Eric Michael Scheffel博士是宁诺人文与社会科学学院经济系副教授。他的研究主要集中在经济学中的计算方法、宏观经济建模、宏观计量经济学和一般时间序列研究以及金融市场分析。

Scheffel博士曾在《应用计量经济学杂志》《期货市场杂志》等高质量经济学和金融期刊上发表多篇论文。

宁诺和人文社科学院介绍
13:30-14:00
迪林勋爵楼 A04
宁波诺丁汉大学是中国第一所中外合作大学，目前拥有约8000多名学生，来自全球70多个国家和地区，国际生占比约13%。2018届本科毕业生中，选择深造的有55.2%进入QS世界大学排名前50的高校。

宁诺采用英国诺丁汉大学教学与质量保障体系，毕业生获得英国诺丁汉大学学士学位证书。在2019年软科中国最好大学排名中，首次参加国内大学排名的宁波诺丁汉大学位居第55名。

人文与社会科学学院（FHSS）是宁诺三大学院之一，目前下设8个本科专业，并提供当代亚、欧洲语言课程的教学。本着开放与实践的理念，人文社科学院致力于培养能适应未来复杂且充满挑战性的国际性专业人才和领导者。根据宁波诺丁汉大学2017-2018学年就业质量年度报告，有超过85%的人文社科学院本科毕业生在毕业后会前往QS（2019）世界大学排名前一百的高校继续深造。


理工学院介绍
14:30-15:30
劳伦斯报告厅
宁波诺丁汉大学理工学院（FoSE）成立于2009年，下设9大院系：建筑和建筑环境系，化学与环境工程系，土木工程系，计算机科学系，电气与电子工程系，地理科学系，数学科学系，机械、材料与制造工程系，以及航空系。学院共开设有15个本科专业，6个硕士专业（授课型和研究型硕士），以及20个博士专业。

学院配备一流师资，引进英式教育体系，采取与英国诺丁汉大学完全一致的教学评估体系，所有课程实施全英文授课，实施小班化教学和个人导师制，充分培养学生的批判性思维、团队协作和独立思考解决问题的能力。

迄今为止，学院有浙江省重点学科1个（机械制造及自动化）、浙江省“十三五”一流学科2个（化学工程与技术、材料科学与工程）。8个本科专业和1个硕士专业获得了国际专业机构/协会的认证。

Faculty of Humanities and Social Sciences & Faculty of Science and Engineering Mini Open Day
19 October 2019
We will introduce the recruitment policy for undergraduate and postgraduate studies in the University of Nottingham Ningbo China (UNNC). You will also have an opportunity to attend some demonstration classes in FHSS and FoSE.

Introduction to UNNC
Founded in 2004, the UNNC is the first Sino-foreign cooperative university in China that has been approved by the Ministry of Education. The University is committed to providing world-class education delivered by world-class scholars. The University currently has more than 8,000 students, who are from over 70 countries and regions. Among the graduating class of 2018 who chose to study abroad, 25.3% entered top 10 institutions in the QS World University Rankings, 55.2% entered the top 50, and 81.7% entered the top 100.

In this presentation, we will introduce the admissions policy and campus life of UNNC, and also answer your questions.

Introduction to FHSS
The Faculty of Humanities and Social Sciences (FHSS) at the UNNC includes four schools and one language centre. Our schools include Economics, Education and English, International Communications, and International Studies. Our language centre focuses on teaching modern European and Asian languages.

Our programmes – at undergraduate, postgraduate, and doctoral level - in International Studies (mixing International Politics and History), International Communications, Education, English, and Economics will help you make sense of the world, understand the problems we face, and equip you with the knowledge and critical skills to contribute to their solution. By combining your chosen programme with a language – you can choose to learn French, German, Spanish, Japanese, or Korean – you will be in a unique position to appreciate the cultural complexity of the modern world; and you will have the opportunity to practice your new language skills during your time at UNNC. With the highest proportion of international students in the University, FHSS offers you a truly global experience. Our students have the opportunity to spend from one semester to up to two years of their four-year degrees at another Nottingham University campus, either in the UK or in Malaysia. Alternatively, you could choose to spend time in one of our many international partner institutions through our participation in the U21 group of world leading universities.

Our graduates enter a wide range of careers that value the kind of student who is curious about the world and seeks to understand and engage with it. It is important to know that you will receive the same degree certificate as any University of Nottingham graduate; and, given that Nottingham is consistently ranked in the top 100 Universities in the world, our graduates are very attractive to employers. We are proud that over 85% of our undergraduate students choose to continue with their education and enter postgraduate programmes in the world’s top universities. Many go on to do PhDs and become the next generation of academic researchers and teachers.

Introduction to FoSE
Established in 2009, the Faculty of Science and Engineering (FoSE) currently has 9 departments and schools: Architecture and Built Environment, Chemical and Environmental Engineering, Civil Engineering, Computer Science, Electrical and Electronic Engineering, Geographical Sciences, Mechanical, Materials and Manufacturing Engineering, Mathematical Sciences and Aerospace.  At present, FoSE offers world-class STEM education, including 15 undergraduate programmes, 6 postgraduate programmes and 20 PhD programmes for doctorate students. Currently, the faculty hosts more than 2600 undergraduate and postgraduate students and about 240 PhD students.

Our academic staff are world renowned experts in their field, and are recruited from top universities from all over the world. All our degree programmes are taught in English, and exams and assignments are submitted in English. Students will benefit from both the classroom lectures and “hands-on” practical experience in workshops and labs. Moreover, 8 of our undergraduate engineering programmes and 1 postgraduate taught programme have been internationally accredited.

Demo Class 1: The fifth generation of mobile communications (5G) – Is it real or just a slogan?
The fifth generation of mobile communications (5G) is viewed as a set of key enabling technologies allowing the realisation of a "hyperconnected society" where billions of users are connected via end devices (e.g. smart home appliances, connected cars, smartphones, laptops) and machines. The technology is seen to allow the seamless exchange data and offer/receive services at a high QoS level. 5G can be considered a set of enabling technologies to support enhanced mobile broadband, massive machine type of communications and ultra-reliable and low latency communications. The lecture will cover the fundamental technology enablers in 5G era, including the comparison of its predecessors (3G-UMTS, 4G-LTE-Pro). The talk also discusses the potential applications of the technology in critical areas such as transportation, healthcare, entertainment and industrial automation.

Speaker: Dr C.F. Kwong
Dr C.F. Kwong graduated with First Class Honours for BEng in Electrical and Electronic Engineering, University of Hertfordshire, UK and a Distinction for MSc in Personal, Mobile and Satellite Communications, University of Bradford, UK. He completed his PhD in Mobile Communications at the Multimedia University, Malaysia.
Before taking up an academic position at UNNC in 2015, Dr Kwong had been a senior lecturer at INTI International University for 15 years, mostly teaching and researching in the field of telecommunication engineering. His research interest includes the heterogeneous networks, mobility management for LTE and 5G, and published a number of publications in journals and conferences in this field. He is currently the Director of Admission and International Relations in FoSE. He is also a member of the Artificial Intelligence and Optimisation research group at UNNC.
Dr Kwong is an active member of the Institution of Engineering and Technology (IET), a Chairman of the IET Malaysia Network Young Professional Section from 2008 to 2010 and a committee member of the IET Malaysia Local Network since 2008. He had been elected as a member of the IET Council in the UK for a three-year term from 2011 to 2014. Dr Kwong is also a Professional Review Interviewer (PRI) on behalf of the IET, interviewing Chartered Engineer and Incorporated Engineer candidates. He is also the IET International Professional Registration Advisor. Most recently he is appointed as a trained IET Academic Accreditation Accreditor.

Demo Class 2 : Media and digital literacies
Media literacy is the ability to critically evaluate media and information in its broadest sense. A media literate person will be aware of media’s influence on beliefs, attitudes, values, behaviours, and the political processes. Digital literates will be able to participate in digital media in wise, safe, and ethical ways. The lecture will offer an introduction to media and digital literacies and show both similarities and differences from each other. Especial attention is given to the question of the blurring line between media consumers and producers.

Speaker: Dr Filippo Gilardi
Dr Filippo Gilardi is the Head of the School of International Communications and the Deputy Director of the Institute of Asia and Pacific Studies (IAPS) at UNNC. His research interests focus on media convergence, copyright protection, and the development of global digital platforms. Dr Gilardi is a Principal Fellow of the Higher Education Academy and a Fellow of the Royal Society of Arts.

Demo Class 3: Is Keynes' General Theory from 1936 still relevant in 2019?
In 1936 John Maynard Keynes published his most provocative masterpiece in macroeconomic theory: "The general theory of employment, interest and money". 
The "General Theory" attacked the prevailing classical macroeconomic orthodoxy at a time of global economic depression. This lecture will provide a succinct summary of the main arguments of Keynes' "General Theory" and discuss its relevance to today's global economic situation.

Speaker: Dr Eric Michael Scheffel
Dr Eric Michael Scheffel is Associate Professor in the School of Economics at UNNC. His research mainly focuses on computational methods in economics applied to macroeconomic modelling, macroeconometric and general time series studies as well as financial markets analysis. He has published a number of papers in high quality Econometrics/Economics and Finance journals, such as Journal of Applied Econometrics, Journal of Futures Markets, Computational Economics, Economic Modelling and Emerging Markets Finance and Trade.

title: 暑期回顾 | 这个夏天，270多名宁诺学子奔赴30多个国家和地区，为了同一个目标
content:
Each year, hundreds of UNNC students choose to volunteer overseas to discover the unlimited possibilities that the world has to offer.
This year, over 270 students set off to volunteer in over 30 countries and regions around the globe.

Please scroll down to read some of the stories. 

· · ·
当一回海外志愿者
是很多UNNCer 大学四年的必选项
今年暑假
270多名同学跨越世界五大洲
前往30多个不同国家和地区
参加海外志愿者项目
他们带回了怎样精彩的经历呢？


◆ ◆ ◆ ◆
“我希望有一天，
所有想读书的孩子都可以如愿以偿”
◆ ◆ ◆ ◆
——陈蕴琦，经济系
 希腊 Greece
如果不是在希腊的将近两个月，我想我可能只会在新闻报道中看到这群难民孩子。

印象最深的是其中一个来自巴基斯坦的男孩。他很好学，也很活泼，会在我们讲课的时候拿出笔记本记下今天的学习要点，还会兴致勃勃地问我们：“你们会给我考试的，对吧。”

＜＜＜＜＜＜＜＜＜＜＜＜＜＜＜

慢慢了解彼此的过程中，我问他是什么让他愿意离开他的父母，只身在希腊雅典停留。他说，因为贫穷，他们家只能供他哥哥去读书，他妈妈只能把他送去学一项传统舞艺，用来补贴家用。但有着一个读过书的哥哥，弟弟怎么也不愿自己的一生只能为别人跳舞，所以愤然离家。但抵达希腊后，同行的舅舅将他一个人撇在雅典，独自去了德国，他被政府收留，靠着救济福利养活自己。好在福利院除了为他们提供食宿外，也教习一些文化课。

他说，他真的很想读书。

我离开希腊的那天，他在电话里哭着问，我们，或者是下一批接班的志愿者们什么时候再能回去教他读书。

我看到的不仅是两代人之间很深的观念断层，以及经济基础跟不上文化需求的矛盾；我也看到了在世界上某些角落，有那么多迫切的，却又无可奈何的对知识的渴望。或许我们能做的真的很少。短短六周只够教授最基础的词汇语法，却有来自七个国家的志愿者愿意为之努力。我相信，一个人的力量很小，世界青年人的力量却很大。
Please scroll down for the English version.
If I had not gone to Greece for the two months, I would have only seen these refugee children in the news.

What impressed me most was a student from Pakistan. Every lesson, he would take notes and ask us enthusiastically, "you will give me an exam, right?"

As we got to know each other, I asked him what made him want to leave his parents and stay alone in Athens. Due to poverty, he said his family could only afford to pay tuition for his elder brother but sent him to learn traditional dance for subsistence. With a brother studying in school, he did not want to spend his whole life dancing for others, so he left. “I really wanted to study”, he told us.

The day I left Greece, he cried and asked when we, or the next group of volunteers, would teach him again.

I felt sorry for him and all the others who are eager for knowledge but have limited access. 

Maybe there is little I can do, but I believe that the power of the world's youth is enormous.

——Yunqi Chen, Year 2 student of Economics



◆ ◆ ◆ ◆
“我们都要学会长大”
◆ ◆ ◆ ◆
——任佳怡，英语语言学与文学系
 摩洛哥 Morocco
七八月的骄阳，25度的晴天，9个人拥挤的公寓，70多个可爱的孩子，4次旅行，无数奇妙的人和事，这大抵就是我在摩洛哥的夏天。
♮
♮
♮
♮
♮
♮
♮
♮
当初选择摩洛哥不是为了完成什么伟大的梦想，而是单纯觉得去非洲是一件很酷的事情，也想借着这次志愿活动体验一个人的生活旅行，告别那个在家人朋友的保护和帮助下无忧无虑成长的自己。

一个人的旅途不算很顺利，甚至在到达后的前三天里，问题源源不断，比如住处频繁断水断电，发生冲突不得不请警察来处理，一个人拖着 23kg 的行李箱爬又高又陡的斜坡。但也就是这三天的奇妙经历，让我开始学着自己去寻找解决方法。

去之前我曾经担心孩子们不配合我上课，而我又没有好的方法去引导他们。但是慢慢发现，他们都很纯真，对外面的世界有无限的憧憬和幻想；每天他们都认真记笔记做练习，因为他们希望通过学到的知识改变自己的命运。慢慢地我也学会了如何为他们准备最合适的教材，尝试着调动课堂的氛围，尽可能帮助到每一个孩子。

回想在临行大会上我给自己定下的两个目标，变得更加有耐心、更加独立，我想我都做到了。感谢这里的一切带给我的成长，尤其是孩子们，他们给了我勇气克服遇到的困难，让我学会用成年人的视角去看待事物。与其说他们感谢我们的到来，不如说我感谢他们在我生命里的出现。


＜＜＜＜＜＜＜＜＜＜＜＜＜＜＜
曾经看过这样一段话：
“长大的意义，大概是有足够的选择权和决定权，有能力分辨外界的声音，愿意从小事中感受美好，在不乐意里发现快乐，慢慢积攒勇气，并且始终保持善良。”

Please scroll down for the English version.
I chose Morocco not to realise any “great dream”, but I simply thought it would be cool to go to Africa. I also wanted to be more independent through this volunteering activity.

But it wasn’t easy. Problems kept popping up, such as the shortage of water and electricity at my residence, conflicts that needed policemen to handle and carrying a 23kg suitcase up a hill. But it was these troubles that made me start to look for solutions by myself.

Before the trip, I had worried that the children would not like me or I would not teach well. But gradually I found out that they were very innocent with unlimited imagination about the outside world. Every day they took notes and practiced questions carefully, because they hoped to change their lives through the knowledge they learned. By the end, I knew how to prepare suitable teaching materials, to moderate a discussion and to help every child as much as possible.

Recalling the two goals I set for myself at the departure meeting - to become more patient and independent - I think I achieved both. I appreciated the children who gave me courage to overcome the difficulties and got me to view things from the perspective of an adult.

——Jiayi Ren, Year 2 student of English



◆ ◆ ◆ ◆
“我的这些第一次，
都留在了安卡拉”
◆ ◆ ◆ ◆
——梅欣哲，国际商务
 土耳其 Turkey
在安卡拉虽然只呆了短短六周，但是每一天都让我感到新奇和陌生。以一个“海外志愿者” 的身份出国，也让我遇见了太多旅程中根本想象不到的事情。

第一次到土耳其，人生地不熟，遇到的挫折更是数不胜数：机场托运的行李箱差点搞丢、项目第一天就在安卡拉市中心迷路、六周换了四个 host family、感冒、中暑......

但其实换个角度想想，每一个挡在面前的阻碍都可以成为攀向更高处的垫脚石，只要能充分利用好它来磨练自己：找不到行李箱就正好锻炼自己在特殊场景下的英语口语，迷路就干脆好好观察土耳其的大街和国内有哪些区别，频繁地换 host family 正是快速结交新朋友的好机会。我想这可能就是拥有一段海外志愿者经历的意义所在吧。

＜＜＜＜＜＜＜＜＜＜＜＜＜＜＜

每段体验都是由外部环境，个人预期和个人行为三部分组成的，如果在外部环境上没办法提升体验感，那就从自身的角度去主动提升项目体验。所以在整个过程中我主动去探索和发现项目内外能带给自己真正成长的东西，也勇敢挑战了一些新鲜的事物：第一次在众人面前用英语表达自己的观点并参与讨论，第一次开 ATV（四轮全地形车），第一次坐滑翔伞，也是第一次因为离别和别人痛哭着抱在一起......这点点滴滴汇聚成了我的安卡拉之旅，平凡却不平庸，至少，这段经历带给我的成长和改变，让我庆幸当初自己做下了这个决定。

＜＜＜＜＜＜＜＜＜＜＜＜＜＜＜


Please scroll down for the English version.
Every single day during my six weeks in Ankara was a fresh experience. Going abroad as an "overseas volunteer" allowed me to explore possibilities that I could not have imagined before the journey.

As it was my first time in Turkey, I was unfamiliar with everything and encountered numerous problems. I almost lost my luggage at the airport, I got lost in downtown Ankara, had four host families in six weeks, caught a cold and so much more.

On the other hand, every obstacle would push a step higher towards achievement. For example, I practiced spoken English while looking for the suitcases, observed the differences between Turkish and Chinese streets and architecture while I was lost, and I had a better chance to make more friends by changing host families.

During my time in Turkey, I also actively tried to explore and discover fresh challenges, such as driving an ATV (four-wheeled all-terrain vehicle) and flying a paraglider for the first time.

This is why having an overseas volunteering experience is important.

——Xinzhe Mei, Year 2 student of International Business



◆ ◆ ◆ ◆
“用六周成为一个热带女孩”
◆ ◆ ◆ ◆
——韩栩，国际商务
 印度尼西亚 Indonesia 
我的家乡是一个北方内陆城市，远离海洋，更缺少一切和热带相关的因素。出于好奇和想要探索的冲动，我搭乘一路向南的航班，来到了坤甸，这个位于赤道的印度尼西亚小城。
＜＜＜＜＜＜＜＜＜＜＜＜＜＜＜

面对这个从未听说，甚至在搜索引擎上都很难查找的城市，我在出行前悄悄把期待值降到了最低，并安慰自己说，这是一个探索当地社会文化的项目，不论条件怎样，都尽力体验和享受吧。但事实证明，我脑中的很多关于这里的猜想，都是错误，甚至是完全相反的。

我原以为印尼是一个落后保守的国家，可来到这里之后，我发现自己对于落后的定义是多么的狭隘。物质上的不足并不能成为衡量是否落后的唯一标准，因为他们的思想是如此包容和鲜活。

生活在一个多元宗教和民族的国家，这里的年轻人对待差异更为成熟，没有排外或敌视，而是积极、友好与好奇。他们和世界上所有年轻人一样，追赶一切新鲜先进的事物，会兴致勃勃地聊起他们心中的潮牌与流行，也愿意成为我们 vlog 中一个略显青涩却热情的身影。

＜＜＜＜＜＜＜＜＜＜＜＜＜＜＜

不同的背景和经历完全不影响我们迅速建立起友谊。我们一起激动地讨论喜爱的偶像、各自的专业，教着彼此各自的母语。不同于中国人的含蓄，他们更主动热情地想要了解、认识新的朋友。在那种真诚质朴的氛围下，拘谨会慢慢消失，好像很容易就能打开心扉。

更多的猜想在这六周中被一个个打破，而它们也时刻提醒我，偏见、不公正的指责、激进的话语是多么可怕的存在。在没有亲身感受过之前，我们没有权利去定义一个人，评判一件事，戴着有色眼镜审视一个国家。

“这里是夏天的老家，有最毒辣的太阳和最凉爽的晚风。”
“赤道上的色彩好像也更鲜艳明亮，云更白，椰子树更绿，夕阳的粉橙更浪漫。”
“渐渐喜欢上坐在摩托后座的感觉，无论是透过头盔可以直视阳光的快感，还是奔驰在傍晚的灌木丛中，享受潮湿空气的凉爽。”
“今天惊喜的碰到了一个会唱中国歌的司机，他的中文磕磕巴巴，却很亲切。”
……
很多回忆都是限量版，人生只有一次机会可以创造。而我很幸运，用六周成为了一个热带女孩，感受并且融入他们的文化，并和这群可爱善良的年轻人共同度过了一个无比难忘的夏天。
Please scroll down for the English version.
My hometown is an inland city in northern China – a world away from the tropics. Curiosity and eagerness to explore took me to Pontianak, a small equatorial city in Indonesia.

I minimised my expectations, as this small city was hard to find even on search engines, but my experience there came as such a great surprise.

I thought Indonesia was a relatively backward and conservative country.  However, everything there told me how narrow my definition of backwardness was – and the young people there were so understanding and passionate.

Like other young people around the world, they are interested in new stuff. Despite our different backgrounds and experiences, we became friends right away. Unlike Chinese - who tend to be more insular - they were more active and enthusiastic to meet new friends.

More assumptions were broken afterwards, which reminded me how terrible prejudice, unfair accusations and aggressive words could be - never define a person or judge someone simply by a stereotype with first-hand experience.

I was lucky enough to spend six weeks as a tropical girl, feeling and integrating into their culture and spending an unforgettable summer with these lovely and kind young people.

——Xu Han, Year 2 student of International Business



◆ ◆ ◆ ◆
“我看到他们眼中泛着光”
◆ ◆ ◆ ◆
——马靖瑄，国际事务与国际关系学系
立陶宛 Lithuania
在立陶宛做海外志愿者期间，绝大多数时间我都与孤儿院的孩子们在一起。

有十六七岁的大男孩，也有七八岁的“小猴子”，他们大都好动、不服管教、只会去做自己想做的事情。我们从来没有将所有人集中在一个教室里过，总有那么一两个经常“失踪”的家伙又去操场或者体育馆了。
♮
♮
♮
♮
♮
♮
♮
♮
在一个非英语国家，面对的又是这样一群年龄差异很大且自小因为自身家庭原因生活在一起的孩子们，我们起初无可奈何，只能借助本地志愿者进行只有是和否的简单对话。那种感觉就好像从几千公里外带着一脑子想法飞到这里后，这里的一切却都在告诉你别想太多你做不了什么。

但是当看到他们努力用拙劣的画技画着自己心中的“super hero”时，当看到他们一个个争先恐后地吃下一大块酸涩的柠檬完成属于自己的“lemon challenge”只为向我们证明这是一个勇敢的小男子汉时，他们的眼里闪着像星星一样微弱却坚定的光。

＜＜＜＜＜＜＜＜＜＜＜＜＜＜＜

其实我们与他们又有何区别，不过都是在自己的年纪努力长大。终有一天，他们会赶上我们今天的步伐，我们也会成为一个新的样子。但你我也都曾经是个孩子，经历过那个眼中泛着光的年纪。只是看到他们，好像曾经自己眼中的光又变得明亮了起来。
Please scroll down for the English version.
While volunteering in Lithuania, I spent most of my time with the children in the orphanage.

In a non-English speaking country, facing such a group of children of different ages who had been living together since childhood, I felt that we couldn’t do much for them at the beginning.

However, when I saw them trying to draw their superheroes and doing the "lemon challenge" (eating a big slice of lemon), their eyes shined like stars - shy but confident.

They reminded me of my own childhood and I realised that there was no difference between us. Looking into their eyes, I became reinvigorated.

——Jingxuan Ma, Year 2 student of International Studies



◆ ◆ ◆ ◆

用一个夏天亲自打破刻板印象
解锁一个陌生国度独有的面貌
这样的经历
你也可以拥有
风里雨里
海外志愿者项目等你


Overseas volunteering is an opportunity to explore and understand the uniqueness of a foreign country and its culture.

If you had an extraordinary summer and want to share, please comment and let us know.

title: 暑期回顾 | UNNCers暑期上辅导班？真相是……
content:
How to make the most of summer holidays is a question all students have to think about every year. Many consider summer school as a wonderful way to practise and learn new skills.

Please scroll down to read the stories of a few students who just finished summer school courses. 

· · ·
新学期已渐渐步入正轨
刚刚过去的这个暑假里
是否有令你回味无穷的经历呢？
其他UNNCers又是如何度过暑假的？

我们采访了几位暑假参加夏校的同学
一起来回顾他们的夏校经历吧


夏校

暑期学校，也称夏校，起始于1871年美国哈佛大学，至今已有近150年的历史。经过多年的发展，暑期学校打开围墙，既面向本国其他高校和社会开放，也向世界开放，努力吸引全世界优秀学子加入。

◆ ◆ ◆ ◆
“开往霍格沃兹的火车上，
我坐在哈利和罗恩的对面”
◆ ◆ ◆ ◆
因为爱好做Vlog和视频剪辑，这个暑假我参加了为期四周的利兹大学夏校，学习电影特效制作。

课程中最有趣的部分是绿幕特效制作。每位同学都在绿幕摄影棚拍摄了短视频，并在教授的指导下通过软件特效把自己加入到电影中。

我和旁边的日本女生都选择了哈利波特片段——开往霍格沃兹的火车上，出现在哈利和罗恩面前的不再是赫敏，而是通过绿幕特效制作上去的我们。通过调整色彩数值，还能使我们的出场看上去更加真实。除此之外，我们还学习了如何在没有画面的情况下通过富有张力的字幕来使音频更加传神等等。

＜＜＜＜＜＜＜＜＜＜＜＜＜＜＜

在进行实地参观时，我们去了位于曼彻斯特的著名的BBC大楼。从BBC 6 Music的演播室，到BBC Breakfast的摄影棚，我们好好地把BBC走了一遍，我还与一位韩国同学体验了BBC Breakfast的模拟新闻播报。

利兹大学是我申研的目标学校之一，这次夏校也算是一次“实地考察”。让我感激的是，尽管我没有选择学校合作项目中的夏校，但依然从学校得到了许多帮助：ESAC tutor Mary老师在我的个人陈述上给了许多建议和帮助；宁诺学生的身份使我不需要提交语言成绩……
——刘心予，英语与应用语言学专业

Please scroll down for the English version.
Because of my interest in Vlog-making and video editing, I attended a two-week summer school at the University of Leeds this July to learn Special Effects in Filmmaking.

The course mainly focused on the use of the software ‘After Effects’ (AE), and I think the most fascinating part must be the green-screen special effects. With AE, I could add myself into famous movies - on the train to Hogwarts, the girl that appeared at Harry and Ron’s compartment door was me instead of Hermione standing there. It was quite exciting and challenging because we were doing exactly what special effects artists would do to make a film.

In addition to lectures and workshops, we also took a one-day trip to the famous BBC building in Manchester. We visited the studios and experienced an interesting mock news report. The summer school experience was like a ‘field trip’ for me since Leeds is one of my target universities for postgraduate study and I really appreciate my tutor at UNNC who helped me with my personal statement. 

Xinyu Liu, Year 2 student of English Language and AppliedLinguistics


◆ ◆ ◆ ◆
“国际记者，
有多肝，就有多精彩”
◆ ◆ ◆ ◆
这次去香港，不巧的是遇上了它的特殊时期，巧的是我去香港大学学习的课程——国际新闻，正好让我有机会从现实中学习，这又何尝不是一个从屏幕和文字之外去了解真相的好机会呢？

幸运的是，新闻里那些闹哄哄的场景我都不曾遇到。或是坐叮叮车穿梭在港片的大街小巷里，或是约上小伙伴在海边喝一杯手冲咖啡，我庆幸自己能体会到这颗东方之珠本该拥有的美好。
♮
♮
♮
♮
♮
♮
♮
♮
夏校在课程设置上，更多是偏向于让学生们体验如何成为一名国际记者，正好与我在学校学习的理论知识形成互补。

我们的授课老师Peter Eng是一名经验丰富的老记者，有次课程中，他要求我们做一个尝试：采访在街上与自己不同国籍的行人，让他们说一说家乡最近的新闻。刚开始时，紧张与焦虑困扰着我，怕尴尬，怕被拒绝……然而真当自己勇敢迈出第一步，才发现这是一件有趣的事情，新奇感远远盖过了原先的不安。原来陌生人并没有想象中那么冷漠，原来世界各地还有那么多我所不知道的事情正在发生。

夏校期间，我们参观了《南华早报》的香港总部、欧盟驻港澳办公室、香港外国记者会，还从BBC、CNN、AFP、Reuters老记者们的对话中了解到，做一名国际记者很辛苦：满世界飞，满地找头发，肝出来的文章要经过层层筛选才能顺利发表。

那为什么还有这么多人选择这个职业呢？

听他们讲述着自己的故事，我心中的这个疑问仿佛也慢慢不问自明：或许，是因为这个职业所带来的精彩人生阅历，以及放不下的厚重的使命感、责任感吧。
——陈奕如，国际传播学专业

Please scroll down for the English version.
This summer, I flew to the University of Hong Kong to study international journalism.

The courses provided students with practical experiences as international journalists, which in terms of curriculum, were exactly complementary to the theoretical knowledge I had learned at UNNC. We spent much time visiting well-known news bureaus and talking to experienced journalists from the BBC, CNN and Reuters.

Our instructor, an experienced journalist, once gave us a “vox pop” assignment to interview random people of different nationalities on the street and ask them about the latest news from their hometown. I was quite nervous about being rejected. However, after the first attempt, everything became different. The strangers were not indifferent at all, and there were so many things I didn’t know were happening all around the world. 

Yiru Chen, Year 2 student of International Communications Studies



◆ ◆ ◆ ◆
未来已来，
人工智能参与法律判决
◆ ◆ ◆ ◆
这个暑假，我在为期一个月的北京大学夏校学习了大数据与网络应用、人工智能与法律两门课程，同时还蹭了Python和ACM-ICPC（国际计算机协会举办的国际大学生程序设计竞赛）的课。

夏校课程学到的知识是对我在学校学习到的一些算法和编程语言的深化，尤其是数据挖掘、博弈论、机器学习，这些是计算机学习中比较深层次的内容，相对来说比较难，每天需要靠咖啡熬过艰难的学习。

＜＜＜＜＜＜＜＜＜＜＜＜＜＜＜

人工智能与法律的课程则为我打开了一个新视角：近年来，法网公开了大量法律数据和审判过程，给机器学习提供了可能，未来人工智能有可能参与到法律判决的过程中，而且现在已经有很多公司已经在开发这样的人工智能了。
——徐浩凯，计算机科学专业

Please scroll down for the English version.
During the one-month summer school programme at Peking University, I studied Legal Intelligence and Networking for Big Data Applications, and also had the opportunity to take a few classes about Python and ACM-ICPC (ACM International Collegiate Programming Contest). 

Those classes deepen my understanding of the algorithms and programming languages I learned at UNNC, especially those about game theory and machine learning. It was a bit challenging to comprehend the new contents at beginning because they were much deeper than I expected. During that period, coffee became a daily necessity for me. 

Legal Intelligence, in particular, opened up my mind – as a large amount of statistics on laws and trials became public in recent years, making machine learning viable. In the future, artificial intelligence might participate in the process of legal judgment. In fact, many companies have already started to develop such kinds of artificial intelligence! 

Haokai Xu, Year 2 student of Computer Science




◆ ◆ ◆ ◆
从喝咖啡喝到吐，
看边际效益递减原理
◆ ◆ ◆ ◆
 “学习是一件持续终生的事。”

这是夏校中老师给我们念叨得最多的一句话。在哈佛大学的50天，我和来自全球不同地方的六七十名同龄人汇聚在同一课堂，大家相互学习、共同讨论。

＜＜＜＜＜＜＜＜＜＜＜＜＜＜＜

我选择学习的课程是微观经济学和Python。特别喜欢微观老师通过个人经历和时事新闻跟我们解释经济原理的方式，有一次他向我们解释边际效益递减，以早晨起来喝咖啡为例，第一杯喝下去神清气爽（还配上他浮夸的演技），第二杯嘛也还可以，但好像没那么好喝，第三第四杯喝完，胃里就在不住地翻腾了……我们立刻就get到了。

教授反复跟我们强调，学经济学不要背，最重要的是理解原理背后的逻辑，要在生活中发现经济学。
——陈怿心，统计学专业

Please scroll down for the English version.
"Study is a life-long process”, my summer school instructor kept reminding us.

During my 50 days at Harvard University, I was glad to have the opportunity to study and talk with around 60 students from various parts of the world.

Among all the professors, my favourite was my microeconomics instructor who always explained economic principles using personal experiences and current events. He once explained the Diminishing Marginal Utility with the example of a morning coffee. The first cup of coffee in the morning would make you feel energetic, but the second might not be as nice. The third might not be attractive at all and after finishing the fourth, you might even feel sick. It was like everyone’s daily routine, so we all laughed and immediately understood the concept.

He also emphasised that we should not learn economics by memorising, but understand the logic behind the principles and find their applications in our lives.

Yixin Chen, Year 2 student of Statistics




◆ ◆ ◆ ◆
学知识、阔视野、遇见优秀的人，
就是这个暑期的意义了吧
◆ ◆ ◆ ◆
这个夏天我通过宁诺和中国银行合作的夏校奖学金项目，前往哥本哈根商学院（世界管理学科前十五院校）学习商业声誉管理学。这门课程侧重商业管理中人文领域的知识，恰好是对我自身偏经济数理的专业学习的补充。

课程中，我不仅了解到了强生公司如何面对“泰诺危机”（1982年，美国有五人因服用泰诺胶囊中毒死亡），更从中深化了对如“危机管理路线图”这种理论知识在实践中的认识。

夏校期间我们还去了丹麦第二大城市奥胡斯，与那里同样在夏校学习的UNNCers一起参访了乐高积木集团总部。
♮
♮
♮
♮
♮
♮
♮
♮
在这之前，我们中的很多人都是家中的独子，有父母无微不至的照顾。而在异国他乡时，大家都激发出独立生活的潜力：做攻略、拍照摄影、采购食材、做饭……回家的途中，万米高空，我望着窗外璀璨星河，感触颇深：“家中，你也许是那习惯了安逸的孩子；可在异国，你只是你。”

我想，夏校的意义，不仅仅在于知识的提升，更是去开阔文化视野和遇见优秀的人吧。
——陈家璇，国际商务与经济专业

Please scroll down for the English version.
In July, I took a course in Reputation Management and Communication at Copenhagen Business School.

The course focused on humanities in Business management, which was exactly a supplement to my major, since business economy focused more on economics and mathematics. 

During the course, I studied the 1982 "Tylenol crisis ", a model for crisis management, where Johnson & Johnson kept the public informed and swiftly withdrew capsules after poisoned packs caused five deaths. In addition to studying real cases, the course also turned theoretical knowledge in my mind such as "crisis management roadmaps” into practical applications. Besides studying, we also went to Aarhus and visited the headquarter of LEGO. 

I think the significance of summer school lies not only in the accumulation of knowledge but also in the broadening of my cultural experiences and meeting excellent people. By studying and living in a foreign country, I gained the courage and independence to endeavour towards my goal fearlessly in the future.

Jiaxuan Chen, Year 2 student of International Business Economy




◆ ◆ ◆ ◆
“抱大腿”中也有博弈论和统计学
◆ ◆ ◆ ◆
这个暑假，我选择了去北京大学夏校学习管理经济学和数据新闻两门课程，前者是和自己专业紧密相关的，而后者则是我感兴趣的。

管理经济学原理干货满满，我们在短短五天时间内几乎学完了曼昆经济学原理的全部内容。最后的结业考试是以小组案例分析的方式进行的，有一个组的同学用博弈论和统计学对“抱大腿”成功率进行了分析，让我佩服不已：他解释说，如果把能力强的人称作“大腿”，把能力弱的人称为“小腿”，在什么样的搭配下，小组的合作更容易成功；他还分析了“小腿”应该如何去做，才能更加容易抱上“大腿”。
♮
♮
♮
♮
♮
♮
♮
♮
数据新闻的课堂也很有意思，我们学习了很多优秀案例，每个小组都做出了一篇数据新闻的报告。有一个小组用动画的形式来呈现世界自杀率增长的问题，让我记忆犹新。

老师还请来了澎湃新闻的专业媒体老师来做评委，有些作业甚至发表在了澎湃新闻上，让我们很有成就感。

这一个月里，我走街串巷，对北京有了更深入的了解，对北京的情感也有由以前的不喜欢变为了向往：有天晚上，我穿高跟鞋坐地铁，一个带着俩孩子的阿姨硬是给我腾出一个座位;我带着两个大箱子换乘地铁，一个陌生人帮我提起箱子下了30多级台阶;和最好的朋友们去景山公园看日落、去胡同里吃烤鸭、看爵士乐演出；在深巷的小馆子里，北京大妞调侃着生活的艰辛，底下一众北漂嬉笑怒骂……

谢谢这个七月，让我在胡同里穿梭、在公交上等待、在人群中寻找，兜兜转转，做了一场真实的梦。
——刘睿皙，金融财务与管理专业

Please scroll down for the English version.
I studied managerial economics and data journalism at the summer school of Peking University. 

Managerial economics is such a strongly practical and intense course that we learnt almost the whole of Principles of Economics in just five days. 

Besides textbook, we also studied many excellent cases of data journalism and each group presented its own work. One group even used animation to visualise the increasing suicide rates all around the world. 

All those creative yet systematic analyses astonished me, and I had a strong feeling of accomplishment that some of our pieces were published.

Everything there made it a perfect summer for me. 

Ruixi Liu, Year 2 student of Finance Accounting and Management

title: 一项“羞涩”的国际大奖：宁诺男生用1美分的卫生巾解决女性困扰
content:
Two proposals that received contributions from UNNC students won awards at the recent 2019 Global Grand Challenge Summit.

(Please scroll down for the English version.)


# 给你24小时，
提出一个应对全球重大挑战的创新项目，
你会有什么样的创意？


这是刚结束不久的第四届全球重大挑战论坛“协作实验室”的限时命题。

宁波诺丁汉大学作为浙江省唯一参赛队伍，共有五名同学前往伦敦参赛。现场，300名来自中美英三国的学生被重新编队并展开协作，宁诺两位同学所在团队从50支队伍中脱颖而出，获得冠军。
沈俊成
及团队成员
何喆帆
及团队成员

 # 现场 # 
1美分卫生巾项目大放异彩 
沈俊成是宁诺商学院金融财务与管理的大四学生。他所在的团队不仅拿到最终冠军，还获得了最受投资者喜爱、最受观众欢迎的创意等荣誉。主持人评价他们时说，“他们真正展示了协作的力量，我特别喜欢这支队伍。”

这支队伍与其他队伍一样，由2名中国学生、2名英国学生、2名美国学生组成。不一样的在于他们的创意：在印度，有约4,300万女性无法负担在生理期购买普通卫生巾的开支，从而引发当地妇科疾病增多。与此同时，全球快时尚产业每年有222,000吨废弃衣服被运到印度帕尼帕特销毁。沈俊成和团队成员将两者做了一个关联，运用科技手段将这些原来要被销毁的衣服在当地消毒，并生产出极具性价比的卫生巾。


这个项目就叫做“从一张卫生巾赋予女性力量”。沈俊成说，灵感来自于队内印度女生谈到的这一社会问题。作为组内唯一一个有商科背景的人，沈俊成负责项目的财务模型，他计算出仅一美分一片的定价，工厂初始投资1.4万美元，年产900万片，即可以实现年利润3.8万美元。同时，他也和同组的两位男生合作设计出了以废弃衣物为原料加工后的卫生巾模型。


“有意思的是，
我们队里三个男生
原来都不知道卫生巾长什么样。
但我们设计出来以后，
组里的女生觉得还挺像那么回事儿的。”
沈俊成有点不好意思地说。

凭借充满想象力的创意、清晰的财务分析和极具操作性的商业模式，目前，这个项目已经陆续收到一些落地的邀约。








我想，它之所以能被这么多人接受，是因为不仅在印度，在全球范围内发展中国家的女性都有这样的困扰，这激起了人们的共鸣。同时，我们的这个解决方案并没有过分依赖科技，相反它并没有很高的技术要求，从而有极大的可行性。”


 # 挑战 # 
24小时、跨文化跨学科 
第四届全球重大挑战论坛由中国工程院、英国皇家工程院和美国国家工程院共同主办，汇集了各界领袖以及新一代工程师和变革者，包括中美英三国工程院领导和院士、决策者、研究人员、创新人员、企业家和新一代工程师，通力创新协作解决未来100亿人口所带来的巨大挑战。“协作实验室”活动是本次论坛的重要环节之一。

经中国工程院邀请，宁波诺丁汉大学作为浙江省内唯一一所参与此次比赛的团队，与包括同济大学、武汉大学等在内的20支中国高校队伍共同出征，代表我国参加本次“协作实验室”活动。

何喆帆是金融财务与管理的大四学生，他所在的团队也拿到了冠军。他们提出了一套患者在家中进行术后恢复的方案。病人自主在家中安装体征监测仪，医生可以通过远程监控进行追踪诊断。这样一来，既节约患者的就医成本，也释放医院的资源。


本次
大赛中，让他颇有感触的是时间的紧迫。“我们要在24小时内想出一个完整的创意和解决方案，并进行演讲和海报呈现。”

在指导老师、宁诺电气工程及其自动化系关秋峰博士（Dr C.F.Kwong)看来，这正是比赛想要传递的信息之一。“要解决100亿人口带来的巨大挑战，留给我们的时间极其有限。”

费哲妮是宁诺航空航天工程大三的学生。她认为跨学科交流是最大的挑战也是最大的收获。“理工科学生对于工程学意义上的美天然会兴奋，但是当将想法带进现实，还需考虑成本、社会效应等等，就需要向商科、社会科学的同学学习。”
费哲妮(中)

这点也得到了两位大赛萌新的认同。来自人文学院经济系的马婧祺和数学系的姜丰才刚刚步入大二，却已经有了与世界顶尖院校学生的交手记录。她们表示，无论是在赛前近4个月的准备期，还是在伦敦短短的10天，都收获颇丰。“不同的文化背景、知识结构的人聚在一起，为了解决一个问题，努力发挥各自的优势”，马婧祺说。

马婧祺
姜丰(右二)

 # 感谢 # 
宁诺培养我解决问题的能力
和协作精神
首次参赛即在世界舞台上斩获两个冠军，这离不开学校学生事务与发展中心、李达三孵化园、创客实验室的支持。五位同学都表达了对学校和指导老师的感谢。

特别谢谢关老师，赛前他每周都指导我们就一个全球性的挑战进行调研、讨论和辩论，这不仅拓宽了我们的知识宽度和深度，也让我们懂得如何面对质疑和不同声音。最重要的是，他一直强调从小处着手，用尽可能简单高效的方式解决问题。” 沈俊成说。

宁诺电子与电气工程系关秋峰博士（Dr C.F.Kwong)说，他很骄傲学生能取得如此好的成绩。在他看来，此次比赛是一次跨文化跨学科的深入合作与交流，传递出一种信息，没有一种文化或一个学科是完全孤立的。拥有对不同文化和不同学科的包容心态，并能从中发挥出自身的创造力，是未来青年应该具备的技能之一。


UNNC student solutions impress at international innovation summit.
 
17-18 September, London: Two proposals that received contributions from University of Nottingham Ningbo China (UNNC) students won awards at the recent 2019 Global Grand Challenge Summit (GGCS). The projects were aimed at improving the gynecological health of women in developing countries and post-surgery recovery respectively.
 
Jointly hosted by the UK Royal Academy of Engineering, US National Academy of Engineering and the Chinese Academy of Engineering, GGCS aims to inspire the next generation of engineers, policymakers and the public to creatively address the pressing issues the planet currently faces, in particular the world population reaching 10 billion by the year 2050.
 
In the Collaboration Lab - in which UNNC students participated – students from three nations with diverse disciplines were required to propose innovative solutions within 24 hours.
 
Team “EmPads”, which included UNNC student Juncheng Shen, proved most popular among the audience as well as investors for its simplicity and potential impact in developing countries.
 
It innovatively proposed that by setting up factories in India to reprocess waste clothes into sanitary pads, it could provide ultra-affordable products as well as numerous employment opportunities for local women.
 
As the only business student in the team, Juncheng applied his UNNC-acquired knowledge to set up a financial model that calculated costs and researched market feasibility, both of which made the proposal stand out.
 
“As waste clothes are usually shipped back to factories in developing countries, enterprises pay no extra charges to send them to us,” he explained.
 
The team is now seeking to turn its scheme into a real-world project with the support of their mentor Jennifer Jia, a scholar of neuroscience from Cambridge University .
 
Fellow UNNC student, Zhefan He played a similar role in another winning team.
 
By combining technologies garnered from data analyses, remote monitoring and community nursing, the team aimed to facilitate greater home-based post-surgery recovery, thereby relieving stress on resources and improving efficiency.
 
He claimed that the biggest challenge was to achieve a breakthrough within the 24-hour time-limit.  “Our mentor required us to set time limits for each session and it was the first time I felt the urgency of having to take action,” he recalled. 
 
Qingqi Ma, Feng Jiang and Zheni Fei, students from the Faculty of Humanities and Social Sciences and the Faculty of Science and Engineering, also took part in the Collaboration Lab. “My take-home message is that multidisciplinary collaboration is an unavoidable trend regardless of one’s academic background,” said Zheni Fei, a student of Aerospace Engineering.
 
Dr Chiew-Foong Kwong, Assistant Professor in UNNC’s Faculty of Science and Engineering, mentored the five students for four months in preparation for the Summit and spoke highly of their performance.
“The Collaboration Lab was not only a competition but rather a multinational collaboration aimed at solving humanity’s problems and raising public awareness of challenges associated with the growing population,” added Dr Kwong.
 
UNNC is highly focused on cultivating student creativity and has been providing platforms to support entrepreneurial goals, such as the Ingenuity Lab, unveiled by Prince Andrew, Duke of York, last year. Along with the Department of Campus Life and Li Dak Sum Incubator, it provided support to this event.



- THE END -

主题示范课程
01

日新月异的信息世界与全球媒体

14:00-15:00
迪林勋爵楼 A05

自19世纪通信技术诞生以来，就一直影响着国际事务，无论是电报的发明、电话的普及，还是如今的推特和微信。

尽管时代和技术在不断变革，我们对媒体和技术所感到的焦虑，与两百年前的人们并无二致。本次讲座中，任格雷教授将给大家展示通信技术在两百年的国际政策和外交中扮演至关重要的角色。

主讲人: 任格雷教授
任格雷教授现任宁诺人文与社会科学学院院长、公共外交学教授。他曾任英国利兹大学传播学研究所所长、国际传播学教授，和英国亚伯大学副校长、国际战略总监。

他的研究聚焦于国际关系和国际传播的交叉领域，并在软实力、公共外交、文化外交、政治宣传、国际传播、媒体与民主等议题上有着丰硕的研究和出版成果。

任格雷教授曾为英国政府撰写英国脱欧后的软实力研究报告，也为威尔士政府的软实力战略提供谏言。他在亚洲多地和澳大利亚持有访问学者身份，是《国际传播》《媒体与传播》等诸多国际知名期刊的编辑、指导委员会委员。

02

零基础西班牙语体验课

15:00-16:00
迪林勋爵楼 A05

西班牙语，也称卡斯蒂亚语，全球约有五亿人使用，主要集中在发源地西班牙和拉丁美洲国家。

按照第一语言使用者数量排名，西班牙语为全球第二大语言，仅次于汉语。西班牙语是联合国的六大官方语言之一，同时也是欧盟、非洲联盟和南方共同市场的官方语言。
 
在本次的西班牙语体验课中，Penélope Franco Estrada老师将会讲解西班牙语的基础发音，并和来宾分享关于西班牙和西班牙语的小知识。

主讲人: Penélope Franco Estrada
Penélope老师出生于墨西哥城，曾在多所墨西哥的大学任教，目前就职于宁诺小语种语言中心，担任主任一职。

至2018年，Penélope老师在宁诺任教满十年。今年，她被评为宁波诺丁汉大学杰出表现奖。

关于宁诺和
人文社科学院
13:30-14:00
迪林勋爵楼 A06


宁波诺丁汉大学是中国第一所中外合作大学，目前在校的约8000名学生来自全球70多个国家和地区，国际生占比约13%。2018届本科毕业生中，选择深造的有55.2%进入QS世界大学排名前50的高校。

宁诺采用英国诺丁汉大学教学与质量保障体系，并且宁诺的毕业生将获得英国诺丁汉大学学士学位证书。在2019年软科中国最好大学排名中，首次参与国内大学排名的宁诺位居第55名。


人文与社会科学学院（FHSS）是宁诺三大学院之一，目前下设8个本科专业，并提供当代亚、欧洲语言课程的教学。学院倾力为学生提供广泛的学科专业课程，和丰富的教学实践、科研机会。本着开放与实践的理念，人文社科学院致力于培养能适应未来复杂且充满挑战性环境的国际性专业人才和领导者。根据宁诺2017-2018学年就业质量年度报告，超过85%的人文社科学院本科毕业生在毕业后前往QS（2019）世界大学排名前一百的高校继续深造。


Faculty of Humanities and Social Sciences Mini Open Day
28 September, 2019

We will introduce the recruitment policy for undergraduate and postgraduate studies in UNNC and FHSS. You will also have an opportunity to attend some demonstration classes in FHSS.

Introduction to UNNC
Founded in 2004, the UNNC is the first Sino-foreign cooperative university in China that has been approved by the Ministry of Education. The university is committed to providing world-class education delivered by world-class scholars. The university currently has more than 7,000 students, who are from over 70 countries and regions. Among the graduating class of 2018 who chose to study abroad, 25.3% entered top 10 institutions in the QS World University Rankings, 55.2% entered the top 50, and 81.7% entered the top 100.

In this presentation, we will introduce the admissions policy and campus life of UNNC, and also answer your questions.

Introduction to FHSS
The Faculty of Humanities and Social Sciences (FHSS) at the University of Nottingham Ningbo China includes four schools and one language centre. Our schools include Economics, Education and English, International Communications, and International Studies. Our Language Centre focuses on teaching modern European and Asian languages.

Our programmes – at undergraduate, postgraduate, and doctoral level - in International Studies (mixing International Politics and History), International Communications, Education, English, and Economics will help you make sense of the world, understand the problems we face, and equip you with the knowledge and critical skills to contribute to their solution. By combining your chosen programme with a language – you can choose to learn French, German, Spanish, Japanese, or Korean – you will be in a unique position to appreciate the cultural complexity of the modern world; and you will have the opportunity to practice your new language skills during your time in UNNC. With the highest proportion of international students in the University, FHSS offers you a truly global experience. Our students have the opportunity to spend from one semester to up to two years of their four years degrees at another Nottingham University campus, either in the UK or in Malaysia. Alternatively, you could choose to spend time in one of our many international partner institutions through our participation in the U21 group of world leading universities.

Our graduates enter a wide range of careers that value the kind of student who is curious about the world and seeks to understand and engage with it. It is important to know that you will receive the same degree certificate as any University of Nottingham graduate; and, given that Nottingham is consistently ranked in the top 100 Universities in the world, our graduates are very attractive to employers. We are proud that over 85% of our undergraduate students choose to continue with their education and enter postgraduate programmes in the world’s top universities. Many go on to do PhDs and become the next generation of academic researchers and teachers.

Demo Class: The Developing Information Landscape: Global media in an ever-changing world

The development of international communications technologies has impacted global affairs since the 19th Century – from the telegraph to Twitter and WeChat. In this demo class, Professor Rawnsley will provide a broad overview of how communications technologies have long been considered an essential part of foreign policy and diplomacy. Demonstrating that the more things change, the more they stay the same, the talk will suggest that the anxieties that rise to the surface today about the impact of communications and media technologies are similar to ideas, fears and suspicions voiced over 200 hundred years ago.

Speaker: Professor Gary Rawnsley

Gary Rawnsley is Professor of Public Diplomacy and Dean of the FHSS at UNNC. His research interest lies on the intersection of international relations and international communications, and he has published extensively on ‘soft power’, public and cultural diplomacy, propaganda, and international broadcasting in world top ranking journals. He recently wrote a report for the British Council and the UK government on British soft power after Brexit and has advised the government of Wales on its soft power strategy. Gary is also interested in political cinema and has co-edited (with Ming-Yeh Rawnsley) Taiwan Cinema, Global Reception and Social Change (2017) and Global Chinese Cinema: The Culture and Politics of Hero (2010). Other prominent publications include The Routledge Handbook of Soft Power (with Naren Chitty, et.al, 2016) and The Routledge Handbook of Chinese Media (with Ming-Yeh Rawnsley, 2015).

Demo Class: Spanish for absolute beginners.

Spanish, also known as Castilian, is spoken by about 500 million people in Spain and Latin American countries. Spanish is the world's second largest language by the number of first language speakers, only comes after Chinese. Spanish is one of the six official languages of the United Nations, as well as the official languages of the European Union, the African Union.

In this Spanish experiential demo class, Penelope Franco will explain the basic pronunciation of Spanish and share some tips about Spain and Spanish with the guests.

Speaker: Penélope Franco Estrada

Born in Mexico City, Penelope Franco works at the Language Centre of UNNC. Penelope started her career as a communicator, journalist and photographer for art festivals. After a few years teaching in different universities in Mexico, she was awarded with a scholarship to study in China. Then, she began her career on language education at UNNC. Currently she is the Director of the Language Centre and has a wide experience in language teaching at different levels and managing commercial projects. Last year, Penelope was recognised for her first 10 years of service at UNNC and this year was awarded as an Exceptional Performer at UNNC.

title: 大一新生简明指南
宁诺版“神奇动物在哪里”，这个少年带来了神农架和九龙峰百余个物种的记录
content:
Luyuan Ge, a Year 4 International Communications Studies student, had a unique experience in old-growth forests, observing and tracing over 100 species of wildlife.

(Please scroll down for more details.)

暑假接近尾声。有人在假期安排了一次难忘的旅行，有人选择埋首于书本，也有人用一段收获颇丰的实习生活充实自己。而在宁诺，有个95后少年，他的选择有些特别。两个月来他深入山林，日出夜归，与飞禽走兽为伴。

他叫葛陆原，是国际传播系大四学生。今年暑假他在神农架桃花源太阳坪保护地和黄山九龙峰保护地参与实习，记录了两地百余种物种。



揭开神农架的神秘面纱

神农架因物种的多样性而闻名。这让对博物学极感兴趣的葛陆原一直很向往。当看到桃花源生态保护基金会招募实习生，他毫不犹豫地报名了。

面试中，有人问他的兴趣点在博物还是在保护？他这样回答，“对我而言，博物不上升到保护就失去了意义，只是给动物带来干扰而已。”凭借丰富的自然观察经验和对野生动物保护的一腔热忱，他入选了最终20人的实习生团队。经过几天的专业培训后，7月初他进入神农架东北部的太阳坪保护地。

葛陆原
葛陆原说，实习工作主要是两部分。一是基础的巡护工作，主要是管控当地的盗猎和乱砍乱伐行为。二是社区工作，包括解决一些放牧问题，摸查潜在威胁人员名单和探索生态产业可能性等。每到天晴，他都会早上七八点就出发，日行8-15公里的山路，到晚饭点才回到保护中心。

近两个月时间，葛陆原在桃花源太阳坪保护区和九龙峰保护地共记录了100多种脊椎动物，包括大约70种鸟类、30种两栖爬行类和10种哺乳类动物。


邂逅天空霸主——金雕

行前，葛陆原很期待能在神农架遇到亚洲黑熊、鬣羚（liè líng）和红白鼯（wú）鼠这些珍稀野生动物。实际巡护中却无一例外地完美“错过”。“有次在巡护途中正面遭遇了黑熊，然而我只看到了下面的树丛，随着熊的奔逃在摇晃”，葛陆原遗憾地说。

鬣羚
红白鼯鼠

但意外的收获也很多。葛陆原说，其中的高光时刻莫过于邂逅天空霸主，国家一级保护动物——金雕。

“当时它在对面山头，翼展特别长，非常雄伟。一开始，我还不能确定是金雕，对过图鉴后确定是亚成年的金雕。”葛陆原说，金雕多见于高山或草原，东部很少见，这次能见到很惊喜。


金雕

夜观中的最大收获则是白头缅蝰（miǎn kuí）。“夜观了五六次，才碰到了这一条蛇。它恰好就在路上，纯黑加上橘黄色的环，很奢华了”。关于蛇，他还遇到了菜花原矛头蝮湖北亚种。葛陆原介绍，蛇是一种胆小的生物。它袭击人都是因为感到生命受到了威胁。他记得自己靠近后，蛇便懒洋洋地摆出S型的攻击姿势，意识到他只想拍照，蛇就继续慢悠悠地走了。
提示：未经专业培训，
请勿擅自近距离接触野生动物

白头缅蝰
菜花原矛头蝮湖北亚种
在结束神农架太阳坪保护地的实习工作后，葛陆原又主动申请去到黄山九龙峰保护地。家在合肥，这次主场作战的他全力协助保护区的物种资料收集工作。不仅发现了蛇雕，刷新保护地新纪录，也见到了俗称“娃娃鱼”的珍贵野生动物中国大鲵。

蛇雕
中国大鲵


渴望未来研究栖息地保护

当然，博物之旅异常艰辛。他的日常，是经历上山被爬虫包围，被蚂蟥咬的恐惧；在人迹罕至的地方踏出路来；时刻留心不让自己滑倒跌落…尽管如此，葛陆原坚定地表示自然观察是他觉得最有趣的一件事。

其实，葛陆原从事自然观察已经有很长时间了。他从小就对动物、对自然充满好奇，进入宁诺后一次海外志愿服务，让他对观鸟产生浓厚兴趣。大一大二他曾在无数个清晨早起观鸟，记录下宁诺校园内的数十种鸟类，甚至发现过国家二级保护动物的身影。即使在英国诺丁汉大学交换期间，这个爱好也从未停止。他在夜间观测时帮英诺发现了定居的赤狐，和被认为已经在校园消失的普通欧螈。

在英诺发现的赤狐

此次在神农架的体验，给予了他更多的思考。“这是我第一次体验野生动物保护这个领域。当然也通过巡护发展了一下自己博物的兴趣。不过像保护区如何与社区融合、如何让社区在支持生态保护工作的前提下从可持续资源中受益这样的命题，是第一次认真地实践和思考。”

他说，本科毕业后打算申研，想要研究的方向正是鸟类栖息地保护，两栖爬行类栖息地保护或是入侵物种防治。尽管本科学习的是国际传播学，与动物栖息地保护这个领域看上去相去甚远。葛陆原给出了他自己的理解：“我觉得我在宁诺学的是一些原理性的东西，更准确地说，是如何理解万物。自然观察可能是我理解万物的另一个视角吧。”


IC student dedicated to conserving “fantastic beasts”

The summer vacation is drawing to a close. Some people arranged unforgettable trips during their vacations, some chose to bury themselves in books, while others enriched themselves with rewarding internships. Luyuan Ge, a Year 4 IC student, had a unique experience in old-growth forests, observing and tracing over 100 species of wildlife.

Famous for its biodiversity, Shennongjia has long been a dream destination for Luyuan. When asked whether his interest lies in wildlife observation or conservation, Luyuan said: “If observation of wildlife can’t be transformed into conservation, then it will be purely disturbance.” As soon as he saw the ad posted by the Taiyangping Nature Reserve at Shennongjia, Luyuan signed up and was selected to be one of 20 interns.

At the reserve, Luyuan’s duties consisted of patrolling, controlling local poaching and deforestation as well as community work such as grazing and listing potential threats. During this time, he had many encounters with rare wildlife, such as a Golden Eagle chick and a White-headed Burmese Viper.“When I encountered the viper during a night walk, it was crossing the road – it looked wonderful with its pure black body and orange stripes on it.” 

According to Luyuan, snakes are timid creatures and only bite when feeling threatened. He recounted a situation where a snake, which had taken up an S-shaped attack position, realised that he only wanted to take pictures. It relaxed right away and continued to slink along the road.

Afterwards, Luyuan continued to do an internship at the Jiulongfeng Nature Reserve in his hometown, Anhui Province, contributing to collecting data and species information.

Although the field trips were tiring, neither playing basketball nor video games were comparably appealing to Luyuan.  “Doing this is extremely relaxing and enjoyable for me.” He took his long-time hobby of wildlife observation into his college life at UNNC, watching and recording birds, amphibians and later other animals at UNNC. During his exchange at the UNUK campus, Luyuan spotted a Red Fox and even a Smooth Newt, which was thought to have disappeared from the area.

Yet Luyuan felt that his experience in Shennongjia gave him a lot of food for thought. "It is my first time to experience wildlife conservation and to have systematic observation; for the first time I started to consider how reserves can be integrated with communities and how communities can benefit from sustainable resources while supporting ecological conservation," said Luyuan.

Luyuan plans to dedicate himself to bird, amphibian and reptile habitat conservation or invasive species prevention after graduation. Although his undergraduate degree in IC would seem to be irrelevant to wildlife habitat protection, he gave his own interpretation -- "I think what I learned at UNNC were principles, or more precisely, how to understand and sympathise in general. Natural observation may be only one of my perspectives to learning about the world."

2009年的9月，理工学院正式成立，下设建筑和建筑环境系、化学与环境工程系、土木工程系、计算机科学系、电气与电子工程系、地理科学系、数学科学系、机械.材料与制造工程系和航空学院九大院系，为国内外的学生提供世界领先的科学、技术、工程和数学（STEM）教育。目前，理工学院提供16个本科专业，6个硕士研究生项目以及20个博士研究项目。
Established in 2009, the Faculty of Science and Engineering (FoSE) currently has 9 departments and schools: Architecture and Built Environment, Chemical and Environmental Engineering, Civil Engineering, Computer Science, Electrical and Electronic Engineering, Geographical Sciences, Mechanical, Materials and Manufacturing Engineering, Mathematical Sciences and Aerospace.  At present, FoSE offers world-class STEM education, including 16  Undergraduate programmes, 6 Postgraduate programmes and 20 PhD programmes for doctorate students.

title: 宁诺教师天团已就位，在线等一个新学期的你
content:
快开学啦


同学们
你们准备好迎接新学期的到来了吗？
UNNC的教师天团可是已经整装待发
就等你们返校了


宁诺现拥有约300名外籍教师，他们来自五大洲的近50个国家和地区。

新学期到来之际，他们已经准备好大礼包，迎接来自全球70多个国家和地区的你们。

The new academic year is approaching and UNNC is ready to welcome all new and returning students. Here you will meet over 300 international staff from nearly 50 countries and regions. 

新学期要到了
来看看老师们对大家有什么寄语吧


“我会把专业知识传授给你们，并教你们在实验中学以致用。每年，我都会带着学生做不同的项目，今年也给你们准备了惊喜哦。

托马斯·爱迪生曾经说过，‘我们最大的弱点就是容易放弃，保证成功的要诀就是永远都再多试一次’。
我想把这句话送给我的学生，你们一定要敢于尝试。我相信胸怀大志，一切皆有可能。”

Ahmed Elamin博士来自苏丹，2014年加入宁波诺丁汉大学，在理工学院从事教学和研究至今，现担任土木工程本科专业的课程主任。

他拥有英国诺丁汉大学土木工程专业的博士学位，他孜孜不倦地为土木工程专业的学生提供优质的教学，并在17/18学年被授予院级奖项——学生最高教学评价奖。

“I like to teach my students the know-how concepts and let them experiment with applications. Every year we do different projects and every year students amaze me with their works.

I’d like to remind UNNC students about what Thomas Edison said one day: Our greatest weakness lies in giving up. The most certain way to succeed is always to try just one more time. You have to try everything, UNNC is full of what you can try, like Robotics classes in our faculty and Climbing walls in Sport Centre. Aim high and the sky is the limit.”

Dr.Ahmed Elamin joined UNNC in 2014 and has been contributing to the teaching and research in the Faculty of Science and Engineering since then. Recently, he has been appointed as Course Director for BEng Civil Engineering programme. He constantly provides high quality teaching to Civil Engineering students and was awarded the Faculty’s Top Students Evaluation of Teaching Award in 17/18 academic year. 


“欢迎2019级理工学院新生，欢迎你们加入理工学院的大家庭。

也希望我们的在校生可以在暑假过后，以更加饱满的姿态开始新学期的学习。
新学年，你们将收获丰富的知识与技能，让你们终生受益。”

杨劼博士2017年加入理工学院数学科学系，现任统计学专业课程主任，主要负责应用数学和统计学专业的专业课以及工程专业学生的数值方法课程。

她擅长将数学理论概念应用到生活场景，不仅方便理解，还为学生带来了愉悦的学习体验。

 “A warm welcome to all the new FoSE students who are joining the UNNC family this semester and greetings to our returning students who are hopefully all feeling well-rested and refreshed after the summer holidays! Here's to a fruitful year of learning invaluable knowledge and skills that will stay with the students long after they have graduated from UNNC! Once a UNNCer, forever a UNNCer!”

Dr.Jie Yang is the Course Director of the Statistics programme from the School of Mathematical Sciences. She has been working at UNNC since February 2017 and has taught a diverse range of modules related to Applied Mathematics, Probability, Statistics and Numerical Methods to both Mathematics and Engineering students. She endeavours to enhance and make the learning experience enjoyable for students through student interaction and showing how theoretical concepts can be applied to real life scenarios. 


“大一新生们，很高兴我和我的同事们能够开启你们充满智慧、冒险又不乏乐趣的学术生涯，带领你们体验苦乐相随的学术之旅。
我希望你们每个人都尽自己最大的努力，不要害怕问问题，成长为有独立人格的人。请记住，遇到的阻碍都是通往更有意义、更幸福生活之路上的垫脚石。”

Greg Bauer来自波兰，是宁诺英语语言教学中心的EAP导师。
 “Together with my colleagues, we hope to offer you a cheerful start with a sense of intellectual adventure and show you that studying, though not always easy, can be a fun and very fulfilling activity.

We expect each of you to do your best, not to be afraid of asking questions, expand and grow as a person and remember that obstacles are only the stepping stones to a more meaningful, and thus happier, life.”

Greg Bauer comes from Poland, and will be teaching academic skills as an EAP tutor at CELE in the upcoming academic year.


“新学期即将到来之际，我想邀请所有新同学与我们一起体验激动人心的全新大学生活。

在这里，你们不仅可以接触到英式教育，而且在大一就能体验创新、收获知识。我期待你们能够挑战自我、广交好友、成为科技领域的未来领袖！”
Sannia Mareta博士，工业机械工程师，来自印度尼西亚，目前在英语语言教学中心教大一理工类课程。

“As an Industrial and Mechanical Engineer, a teacher and a PhD Graduate from UNNC, I'd like to invite all students to take part in the very mind-blowing and game-changing experiences with me and the team this coming academic year; here you would not only be exposed to the British education style, but also to witness how innovations, creations and knowledge are initiated from your very first year. My expectation for you is to be able to challenge yourself, make as many friends as possible, and be the future leaders in science and technologies!”

Dr.Sannia Mareta is from Indonesia and currently teaches preliminary year Science and Engineering courses at CELE.


“亲爱的同学们，我很期待与你们相见，带领你们在UNNC开启一段刺激又充实的学术旅行。

很荣幸能给你们上课，带你们深入了解历史的复杂性和东西方之间的差异与关联。
我在新学期为大家准备了惊喜，打算和同学们一起对历史话题进行更多探索，大家可以对新学期的课程有所期待;)”

Christian Mueller来自德国，曾经在德国、英国学习，会说七门外语。他来UNNC已经五年了，目前在国际事务与国际关系系教授历史学相关的课程。

"Dear students, I very warmly welcome you to an exciting and rewarding journey at UNNC. First and foremost, do enjoy your time as active students at UNNC. It is a unique place of learning like no other. I very much look forward to meeting you all in the coming four years and stimulating your academic journey through the realms of history and your exchange journey abroad in year 3. It will be my pleasure to teach you and to give you a deeper understanding of the complexities of history that show the constructive connections and entanglements between West and East. My students will love to hear that we will interpret and discuss together more primary history sources than ever before. The surprise will be how we do that...
With all my best wishes, Christian"

Dr. Mueller is an Anglo-German scholar with teaching and research experience in many countries around the world, and speaks around 7 modern languages. He is now going in his 5th year as Associate Professor in History at UNNC. Dr. Mueller will be teaching on different modules in history within the school of International Studies next semester, and will host three full modules in the spring.


“下学期我会教授一门三年级的课程——文化分析，在这个课程中，你们将对不同文化有所了解，并用此来解释不同文化下人们的行为。

我想你们可能会被我的教学风格震惊到……因为我打算尝试不对着PPT讲解，而是直接跟你们进行交谈式教学。
欢迎来到宁诺！希望你们能喜欢这里，多多交朋友，找到自己的学习兴趣。”

Mary Ainslie来自英国，曾在泰国、马来西来、中国等亚洲国家生活多年，2011年加入宁诺，现任电影与媒体研究副教授。

"Congratulations on coming to Nottingham! Make sure that you enjoy yourself, make plenty of friends, take an interest in learning, and don't worry about your grades. Perhaps students will be 'surprised' by my teaching style - I try not to use PowerPoint slides and prefer to talk directly to them - this is a far better way to learn."

Dr. Ainslie is from the UK, but has lived in Asia for a long time, mostly in Thailand. She has been at the University of Nottingham since 2011. Next semester she will be teaching the year 3 module 'Cultural Analysis', in which students will learn about the different understandings of culture and how to use these to interpret their own environment.



“热烈欢迎宁诺新生，你们即将融入这里，并成为这个出色的学院的一部分；衷心欢迎返校学生再次回到宁诺，迎接全新的经历。

我们希望每位学生都能发现并利用好学校提供的资源和机会，在这里获得独特的体验。”
Paolo Bianchi博士来自意大利，是宁诺商学院经济学助理教授，也是国际商务经济学项目主任。他于2009年9月加入宁波诺丁汉大学，教授本科生和研究生经济学和计量经济学。

Bianchi博士的教学目标是让经济学和统计学的概念易于理解，并鼓励学生们通过联系生活经历快速掌握知识。他的课堂形式包括小团体和大团体的师生互动，学习方式丰富多样、过程充满乐趣。

“A cheerful welcome to all new Nottingham University Business School (NUBS) China students that will be soon discovering ways to get involved and become part of this outstanding community and a heartfelt welcome back to the returning students ready for again another year of a life-changing experience here at UNNC.”

Dr.Paolo Bianchi is Assistant Professor in Economics. He has been working at UNNC since September 2009, and has taught in Economics and Econometrics modules both for undergraduate and postgraduate students. Dr. Bianchi aims to reach each learner, novice or expert alike, by making economics and statistical concepts accessible and relevant to their lived experiences. His classes involve teacher-learner interactions in both small and large groups making the learning process transformative and enjoyable. 


“热烈欢迎新生们和返校学生们进入新学年！我希望你们能在大学里度过一段美好的时光，并充分利用学校能为你们提供的一切资源。

没有什么事情是一蹴而就的，你们必须付出很多努力才能在学习和工作中取得成功。但请不要忘记，我们将随时随地为你们提供最有力的支持。”
Marina Glushenkova博士来自俄罗斯，是宁诺商学院经济学助理教授。她自2016年10月加入宁波诺丁汉大学，并教授本科生以及研究生商科课程。

她在课堂中使用数字交互，在模块中引入混合学习元素，在教学中结合理论和实际案例研究，为学生创造更有效、更舒适的学习环境。Glushenkova博士的研究兴趣主要集中于国际宏观经济、金融和电子商务领域。

“I gladly welcome the new entrants and our returning students to the new academic year at the UNNC! I hope you will enjoy your time at the University and take a full advantage of everything UNNC offers. Don’t forget that nothing worth doing is easy, and you must put a lot of efforts to succeed in life and study. Please know that the NUBS China team is always available to support you on the journey to success.”

 Dr.Marina Glushenkova is an Assistant Professor in Economics from NUBS China. She has been working at UNNC since October 2016 and has taught a range of modules at different degree stages to the business students. She tries to create more effective and comfortable learning environment for students through usage of digital interaction in the large classroom lectures, introduction of blended learning elements in her modules, and combination of theory with practical case studies in her teaching. 

今天是教师节
你有什么话想对你的老师说呢？
你和UNNC老师之间有什么样的故事？
你心目中的好老师是什么样的？
你对新学期的课程有什么期待？
快来留言区与我们分享吧！
10th September is Teachers’ Day in China. Is there anything you want to say to your teachers? What is your expectation for the modules of the new term? What do you think makes a good teacher? Please comment and share your story with us.

title: 欢迎来到宁诺新手村，你的大护法已在此恭候多时
content:
宁波诺丁汉大学2019级萌新们
再过不久，你们就要入学了
当你迈入宁诺新手村
一定会发现这里的学习环境跟之前有所不同
尤其是面对全英文的教学时，肯定有不少同学会问：
我真的可以适应吗？

在此恭候多时的宁诺新手村大护法——
英语语言教学中心（CELE）有话要说：
“听我的，没问题。”


宁波诺丁汉大学英语语言教学中心（Centre for English Language Education, CELE）为每位即将启程的萌新配备了六大法宝，帮助大家掌握学术英语、融入全英文的学习环境中，为今后全面、系统、深入地进行专业学习打好基础。

从高中到大学、从以往的学习环境到国际化全英文学习环境，CELE将陪伴新同学们度过大一这个重要的“转变年”。

CELE宣传视频


Scroll down for English version

The new academic year is coming soon and UNNC is ready to welcome all students. New students must be curious and nervous about the prospective study and life at UNNC, as English will be the official teaching language here. Considering also the significance of the transition between high school and university, the University constructed the Preliminary Year Programme and new students will spend their first year in CELE, the Centre for English Language Education.

Please scroll down to learn more about how UNNC and CELE support new students to smoothly integrate into the English-speaking environment and be well-prepared for further study.



法宝一：
来自全球16个国家和地区的资深教师团队
No. 1: Experienced tutors
宁诺英语语言教学中心是全球规模最大、教学质量最高的英语语言教学机构之一，现有教师近110名，他们来自五大洲的16个国家和地区，其中大部分老师来自英国。

每一名老师都具备优秀的专业素养和丰富的教学经验，践行“以学生为中心”的教育理念，更重要的是他们十分了解中国高中生的英语水平，能够一步步带领同学们掌握相关的学术技能，逐渐适应全英文的学习环境。


Scroll down for English version
CELE is one of the largest and most well-established English language teaching departments in the world. It has about 110 tutors, coming from 16 countries and regions, with the majority being from the UK. The highly qualified and “student-centred” tutors are also experienced in English teaching in China. 

Through the Preliminary Year Programme, they will guide new students to gain academic knowledge and skills as well as to gradually adapt to the study environment.


法宝二：
循序渐进的课程设置
No. 2: Step-by-step courses
一年级课程的主要目的是衔接高中与大学，帮助新生更好地完成专业学习。

大一学年分为上下两学期，每学期包含两门学术英语课程和两至三门专业基础课程，英语课与专业课的配比基本达到1：1。学术英语课程从听说读写入手，全面提高学生的英语能力和学习技能；专业课程则从基本概念与原理入手，为学生将来深入学习专业知识夯实基础。

课程难度循序渐进，以学术英语课程为例，第一学期所有学生都学习同样的两门课，着重听说读写的技能与表达；而第二学期的学术英语课程则会根据所学专业进行文理分科，偏重专业领域的学术英语和口语表达。


Scroll down for English version
The Preliminary Year Programme aims to equip new college students with necessary knowledge and skills for the coming years. Each term students will take two English for Academic Purposes (EAP) modules to practice language skills as well as two to three content modules of their courses. All modules are designed in a step-by-step structure. 

For example, EAP modules will be the same for all students in the first term, but specified for students of different courses in the second term.



法宝三：
完善贴心的导师制度
No.3: Professional tutorials
除了日常的课程，CELE还为大一新生们安排了学术导师和个人导师。

定期举行的学术导师见面会可以是一对一的单独见面，也可以是同班4-5名同学与导师共同见面。面谈主要围绕近期的某项学业任务展开，比如讨论最近在写的论文构思。同时，同学们还可以向学术导师咨询一些学习上的困惑，请教学习建议等。学术导师负责解答同学们与学术英语课程相关的问题，专业课的问题则由课程主管来负责解答。

个人导师见面会通常是一对一的形式，每次至少15分钟。讨论内容主要是关于个人生活方面的，例如是否适应宁诺的生活，与同学、室友的相处是否融洽等等。个人导师见面会通常由学生主导，由学生决定讨论话题；每个导师都会遵守保密原则，与学生之间的面谈内容将会严格保密。


Scroll down for English version
In addition to the timetabled classes, Year-1 students are required to attend a number of academic and personal tutorials during the year.

There will be regular academic tutorials throughout the year, which may focus on a particular aspect of current work, like a coursework plan or draft. 

Tutorials are also an opportunity for students to ask any academic related questions, including but not limited to assessments, group projects, or feedbacks on papers.

Personal tutorials usually focus on non-academic perspectives. They are student-led, one-to-one meetings to ensure students’ personal wellbeing. Students are free to decide what to discuss or share, like difficulty in making new friends or activities of student organisations. All discussions between students and personal tutors are confidential.




法宝四：
小班化的教学模式
No. 4: Small-sized class
学术英语课程一般是每班18个人，因此老师们可以充分照顾到每一个学生，根据学生不同的学习需要给予指导。

例如写一篇论文，老师们会将这项任务分解为不同的阶段，包括如何阅读参考文献、如何做笔记、如何列提纲、如何写草稿、如何做引用等等。在每个阶段，老师们都会给每个学生针对性的反馈和意见，指导学生们完成论文。


Scroll down for English version

The class size of EAP modules is 18 in average. This means better communication and interaction with tutors. 

Tutors will pay more attention on each student's individual performance. For example, tutors will give feedback and advice based on each student’s performance and needs in each stage of a writing task. 



法宝五：
来自学术指导团队的全方位支持
No. 5: Coaching and Support (CAS) 
如果学生在课堂之外需要额外的英语学习支持，CELE下辖的学术指导团队（Coaching and Support, CAS）将提供各种各样的语言学习帮助。

CAS团队由教学经验丰富的老师组成，组织一对一语言指导、研讨会、讨论小组、在线学习和讲座等一系列活动。他们为大一学生提供英语语言和学习技能方面的支持和指导，让同学们能够更好地融入英语学习环境。


Scroll down for English version
The CAS team of CELE provides extra English language and study skills support and guidance for Year-1 students in need. 

Students can participate in a variety of activities such as one-to-one advising, workshops, discussion groups, and online paraphrasing and self-study opportunities to improve various perspectives of their language skills. 


法宝六：
严格的考勤制度
No. 6: Strict attendance policy 
宁诺大一学年的课程都是必修课，严格的考勤制度将监督每位萌新好好学习。

缺勤累计到达一定次数将会获得书面警告、被主管老师约谈、被中心主任约谈等“特殊待遇”。如缺席情况严重，甚至有可能被取消考试资格。


Scroll down for English version
Attendance as well as engagement is closely related to academic performance. All classes in preliminary year are compulsory and attendance will be recorded for all scheduled classes and tutorials. 

For example, serious non-attendance cases will be reported to tutors in Department of Campus Life (DCL), CELE Student Engagement Officers and ultimately Head of CELE, or lead to failure of the relevant modules. The policy aims to ensure students are engaging appropriately with the University. 



六大法宝助你一路披荆斩棘
你只管奋力向前，我们为你保驾护航
收拾好行囊，我们一起出发吧！

UNNC will work hand in hand to make your first year smooth and fruitful. Thus don’t worry, be positive and do your best.

title: 表白公益小王子衷浩：难民看护、环境治理……这个小伙子思考的是全人类
content:
Hao Zhong, who has just graduated with a degree in International Studies, is someone who appreciates the beauty of nature. From volunteering with an NGO to supporting sustainable development, Hao aims to gain an insight into how to become a visionary citizen of the world.

(Please scroll down for more details.)

“那些感受环境之美的人们，能从中获得生命的力量，直至一生。”蕾切尔·卡逊在《寂静的春天》里如此写到。

衷浩就是这样一个感受环境之美的人——去黑龙江保护湿地、去哥本哈根看护难民、去台湾做田野调查…他想从中获得力量，找到最佳的生命状态。刚刚从国际学专业毕业的他，如愿进入国际环境NGO(Non-Governmental Organization，非政府组织)“根与芽”上海办公室从事环境教育。

上周衷浩随同事在内蒙古通辽市做生态调查，12年间，当地与根与芽合作种树超200万棵。这是2016年与2019年的对比图。



因为热爱，所以去做
为什么会对环境公益产生浓厚的兴趣？衷浩一时也答不上来。

“从没想过是因为什么，也没想过它会为我带来什么，只是觉得我喜欢，并且能从中获得意义感。”他还谈到儿时的经历，看到水龙头一直开着，他会主动去关上，“那个时候就觉得，我们在浪费水的时候，非洲还有很多人用不上干净的水。”在那样的年纪就有这样的世界公民意识，衷浩与环境公益的缘分似乎是注定的。

第一站：哥本哈根
衷浩对于公益的第一次深度体验，就发生在他大三丹麦交换时的哥本哈根难民看护中心。

“当时觉得这是一份可以很直观地了解到欧洲难民群体的工作，所以就去了。”在看护中心的工作繁复而又琐碎，工作时间从晚7点到第二天早7点，两人通宵守夜。工作内容包括准备早晚餐、打菜、洗碗、分配床位、分发衣物等等。

其中，床位抽签的环节让衷浩感触良多。由于难民人数多于床位，所以需通过抽签决定，没有抽中的只能睡地上或者另寻他处。结束工作回家的路上，衷浩时常能在路上遇见一些人席地而睡。

哥本哈根难民中心


“看到这些略感无力，自己现在并没有能力作出什么改变。但也正是看到世界的不完美和不公平，我才更有动力去行动。”


在难民看护中心的时光有苦有甜。遇到过掌握多语种的志愿者、曾与中国人做过生意的难民等等，这些都让衷浩感到新鲜和有趣。

“但危险也存在，有一次一位难民因为来晚，吃不到饭菜，很愤怒，甚至同其他人发生了流血冲突。”美好的回忆成为了他前进的动力，危险的情况也没能阻挡他走下去的脚步。

衷浩在丹麦的农场中工作

第二站：北京
交换结束之际，衷浩看到了北京一家环境NGO创绿研究院的实习生招募信息。衷浩对这个能让自己公益情怀“落地”的实习异常感兴趣。不过面对用一个间隔年实习的决定，他起初还是犹豫的。一边是积极准备读研、找工作的同级同学，一边是他热爱的可持续事业。



“我还是不希望放弃这个机会。”他说，“想到我从小学不停地上到大学，如果去体验另外一种生活方式，同时停下来对自己十几年的学生生涯进行反思也未尝不是一个好的选择。”
最终衷浩选择了间隔年(Gap Year)，如愿加入创绿研究院，成为气候与能源项目组一员。

这是一家政策倡导类的环境公益组织，通过政策研究、时事热点分析和研究、与促进利益相关者的跨界对话等方式，间接推动公共政策的制定向更可持续化的方向转变。

第三站：黑龙江、台湾
Gap year快结束时，他又去参加了世界自然基金会（WWF）黑龙江流域的湿地保护项目，在大东北保护湿地的同时，也为那里的孩子们上了一堂堂生动的环境教育课。

衷浩跟随WWF在黑龙江做环境教育志愿者
今年寒假，衷浩跟随“扶风计划”到台湾做田野调查。在这里他接触到多位90岁高龄的老人。“他们当时大多生活在社会边缘，唯一的信念就是回到大陆的家乡，谁知一等就是40年。”衷浩无不惋惜地说，“难以想象如果我的一生也这样度过会是怎样？”时至今日再谈起这段经历，衷浩的声音仍有些哽咽。

下一站：“努力看到这个世界真实的一面”
上月中旬，衷浩前往南开大学参加中国国际公务员能力建设项目培训。该培训校内报名踊跃，竞争十分激烈。

“从当前国际形势、中国的多边外交、北极形势到联合国模拟招聘、联合国翻译等，每天都在汲取新知识、获得新体验。感受最深的是‘联合国视角’，培训中有现在或曾经在联合国工作的老师参与进来，分享他们的故事。他们看待一些世界性问题的角度非常值得思考。”
“我想尽力去冲破国界、种族、阶级、宗教等阻碍我见识这个世界的因素，去看别人是如何生活、思考的，努力还原这个世界真实的一面。”

衷浩在河南支教


我不想成为一个愚昧的人

“愚昧有两种，一种是无知，还有一种是与世隔绝，无论哪种，我都不希望自己成为一个愚昧的人。

许多问题并非不存在，只是受限于视野。也许我们脚底下踩着的木地板，是非法采伐自太平洋某岛国原住民赖以生存的原始森林呢？可能我们随手丢出去的垃圾最终以其他形式又回到我们生活中呢？

呼吸新鲜空气、喝干净的水，这本应是基本的人权，然而现实却不是。所以我想用自己的行动带来影响，最终促成改变。”


这是支持衷浩在公益之路越走越远的最大动力。

衷浩在印尼支教
当然，在衷浩的可持续事业之路上，也有很多人给予支持。“比如交换前，系里的Christian Mueller博士在了解我的想法后很支持我，为我撰写推荐信、提供很多关于丹麦的信息，对我帮助很大。”
衷浩在获得实习金像奖时分享经验
回顾五年的大学，衷浩总结说：“‘内心丰盈、积极行动的未来公民’是我在大学期间长期探索后找到的最契合本意的成长原则。”

他笑道，“我一直希望去探索更多可能性，拓展生命的宽度，找到最佳状态，这样等我60年后感叹岁月不饶我时，还能有后半句——好在我也未曾饶过你啊，岁月。”

(Please scroll down for more details.)

NGOs and environmental protection - this young man thinks of all mankind

“Those who contemplate the beauty of the earth find reserves of strength that will endure as long as life lasts,”Rachel Carson writes in Silent Spring. 

Hao Zhong, who has just graduated with a degree in International Studies, is someone who appreciates the beauty of nature. From volunteering with an NGO to supporting sustainable development, Hao aims to gain an insight into how to become a visionary citizen of the world.

When asked about his interest in public welfare, Hao says: “I have never thought about what it can bring me. I just feel content and pleased to do these things.” He also talks about his awareness of environmental protection since childhood – “Just think about billions of people suffering from water shortages before we waste water.”

The experience that affected Hao the most was being a volunteer at a refugee care centre in Copenhagen during his exchange in Denmark. His chores included preparing food, washing the dishes and distributing daily supplies. 

“I met multilingual volunteers and refugees who had done business with China; once I even saw bloody conflict in the centre,” says Hao. “I understood that I personally may not make a difference, but it was also the imperfection and inequality of the world that motivated me to act.”

While other Year 4 students were considering pursuing a Master’s or preparing for job interviews, Hao noticed an intern opportunity at an NGO in Beijing. Despite the peer pressure, Hao chose to spend a year devoted to sustainability – “I have been studying since primary school. Maybe it’s time to stop to experience another life and examine my gains.”

Hao interned in Beijing, participated in a World Wildlife Fund wetland conservation programme in Heilongjiang Province, and went on to perform field research in Taiwan. "I want to try my best to break down the barriers of national boundaries, race, social class, religion and other factors that impede my understanding of the world, and to see how other people live and think." This is Hao’s greatest motivation on his road to improving public welfare.

“International Studies gave me exactly what I needed - it provided me with international vision and my instructor, Dr. Christian Mueller has been very supportive and gave me professional advice,” says Hao.

Hao has since started a new journey as a member of Shanghai Roots & Shoots, a non-profit programme started by the renowned primatologist Jane Goodall. When looking back at his college life, Hao summarises that he has clarified his pursuit to become a visionary citizen with inner richness and active participation “to explore the endless possibilities and expand the breadth of life, so that 60 years later I will have no regrets.”

title: 【致新生家长】宁诺二三事，快速了解孩子将要入学的地方
content:
致：宁波诺丁汉大学2019年国内(高考)新生家长
亲爱的家长，祝贺您的孩子成为宁波诺丁汉大学的一员。

您在帮助孩子选择大学的时候，可能已经了解宁诺是一所非常特别的大学。它是中国第一所中外合作大学，教学的语言是英语，本科学生完成学业后获得英国诺丁汉大学学士学位。

正因为宁诺采用英诺的教学与质量保障体系，大学的教学管理和制度，和国内传统大学相比，有一些不同之处。

我们给您寄送《家长指南》和发布这篇文章的初衷，正是希望更好地帮助您了解宁诺的特殊性。对您的支持和理解，我们深表感谢。

To UNNC parents: 

Congratulations to you and your children! As you may already know, UNNC is a Sino-foreign university - English is our official teaching language and students graduate with University of Nottingham degrees. At first, therefore, UNNC may appear a little challenging for new students and their parents who are used to a more traditional Chinese model of education. 

You may have concerns about module selection, exchange opportunities and the career development of your children. Here is some useful information and advice for you to better understand UNNC and better support your children as they kick-off this new phase of their lives.

 学 制 

英国大学的本科学制是三年。为与我国高等教育学制保持一致，同时兼顾英语技能的提升，宁诺的本科学制是四年。

大一，教学形式主要是20人左右的小班课，学习学术英语（EAP）课程和专业入门课程。虽然大一各科成绩并不计入最后的学位等级，但是如果不能通过考试，学生将无法升入二年级。

大二，英国大学中称作资格年（Qualifying Year），课程设置开始与英国诺丁汉大学一致。大二学年的各课成绩仍不影响最终的学位等级划分，只要达到课程要求，学生便可升入三年级。但是，大二第一学期的成绩将作为学生申请海外交换交流项目的重要依据。

大三与大四，英国大学中称作第一部分与第二部分 （Part I and Part II）。学生在此期间获得的成绩，将用于最终的学位等级划分。


 学 位 

和中国大学颁发的学位证书有所区别的是，宁诺所颁发的英国诺丁汉大学学士学位证书上会注明学生的学位等级，等级共分为四等，即一等、二等上、二等下或三等学位。学位等级评定可能会影响学生升学院校的选择。
• 平均分70分及以上属于一等学位；
• 平均分60分及以上但低于70分属于二等上学位；
• 平均分50分及以上但低于60分属于二等下学位；
• 平均分40分及以上但低于50分属于三等学位；
• 平均分低于40分无法获得学位。


评分体系

宁诺采用的是英国大学的评分体系，虽在世界上已被广泛认可，但与中国传统高校相比有着很大的区别。考试通过的成绩为40分。这个分数听起来也许很低，但在英国大学里，这是很正常的得分。

40分以上属于合格的成绩，50分以上属于较为满意的成绩，60分以上属于好成绩，而70分以上已经达到优秀。学生必须学习非常努力才能取得70分或更高的分数。


信息保密

在宁诺，我们都尊重一个事实，即我们的学生都是成人。

这就意味着，根据诺丁汉大学的相关规定，未经学生本人同意，学校任何一名教职员工都不会同家长讨论学生的学习情况，包括透露学生的成绩。我们希望学生能与父母进行直接沟通，对自己的学业负责，而不是由父母到学校来代办。


海外学习

海外暑期项目 
暑期海外项目旨在帮助学生更好地了解世界，通过亲身体验海外名校的学术文化氛围，提高自身学习及研究能力。

海外暑期项目通常在每年的6-8月进行。目前宁诺与英国、挪威、美国、韩国等各地的院校均有海外暑期项目合作，向所有学生开放。

交换生、海外学习项目

学校为学生提供一定数量的交换生出国机会，符合要求的大三学生可以前往英诺或其他海外合作院校进行为期一学期或一学年的学习。交换生项目不需要追加学费，学生需自理来回机票与在海外的住宿和生活费。

除交换生项目外，学生还可以申请海外学习项目，前往英诺或其他海外合作院校进行为期一学期或一学年的学习。学生需要支付一定的海外院校学费，同时自理来回机票与在海外的住宿和生活费。


沟通渠道

宁诺会为每位学生安排一名个人导师（Personal tutor）。这些个人导师来自教学团队，学生在学习或生活上遇到困难时，可以向他们寻求帮助。

每学年，个人导师与学生至少要见面两次。当然，学生也可以在其他时间要求与导师见面。每位导师每周固定两小时在办公室，该时段学生可以随时找导师进行交谈。同时，学生也可以在其余时间约见他们，但必须提早进行预约。
除了个人导师外，学校还为每位学生安排一名辅导员，并根据实际情况配备朋辈导师，为学生适应与成长提供全方位的支持。辅导员将和个人导师、副舍监(由学术教师担任)、朋辈导师一起，通过关怀服务、非正式教育课程、丰富多彩的活动，促进学生在认知、情感、社会性等诸多方面多维度的成长，进而丰富学生的校园生活体验和提升学生的综合素质。

就学期间，学生若需要任何心理层面的支持，也可以与心理咨询中心（University Counselling Service）联系，中心有专职心理咨询师提供安全、保密的中英文咨询服务，协助学生处理人际、学习、生活等方面的压力和心理困扰，帮助学生维持身心平衡与心理健康。
另外，学生将选举代表，出席师生协商委员会（Learning Community Forum），与教工成员一起讨论学生可能遇到的困难。如果任何问题在师生协商委员会上得不到解决，问题将继续反映到学校的管理层，由管理层作出相应答复。

此外，宁诺还通过学生问卷调查（学生教学评估SET和学生课程评估SEM），定期对学校所有的课程与老师进行评估。这些问卷信息都是保密的。


特殊需要

宁诺残障支持团队为有特殊需求的学生提供全方位支持和专业建议。同时，各学院及相关部门设有专门负责联系特殊需要学生的老师（Disability Liaison Officer），对于有特殊需求的学生，他们会根据残障支持团队对学生评估后的建议作出相应的特殊安排。

有特殊需要的学生可在入学后尽快联系相关老师，以便学校及时作出相应的安排。学生的个人信息会严格保密。

 转专业申请开放时间：一年级第一学期期末
 转专业结果公布时间：一年级第二学期第一周



从大一开始规划职业发展
合适的职业

宁诺鼓励学生从大一开始规划职业发展。选择合适的工作不仅要考虑专业与职位的相关度，更要关注自身性格、兴趣和技能等因素的匹配度。

此外，学生需要通过实习实践活动了解行业特征、职位要求、企业文化等外部工作环境。只有合理安排大学生活，学生才能更快地找到合适的工作，实现人生理想。


阶段规划

我们通过全程化的就业指导体系，引导每个年段的学生拥有明确的职业发展目标。
大一：培养明确的职业规划意识，尽早开始规划职业。
大二：根据自身的特点探索行业状况，决定毕业后是否就业或升学。
大三：通过参与实习实践活动提高就业竞争力，并完成各项就业升学相关考试。
大四：把握最佳申请应聘时机，获得合适的就业和升学机会。


就业指导与服务

 诺丁汉卓越奖课程：宁诺开设的诺丁汉卓越奖课程旨在培养雇主所认可的各项就业能力。学生通过选修不同的课程，提高企业所看重的能力， 如领导力、团队合作能力、独立工作能力等就业通用技能。

 就业指导咨询服务：学生可通过预约专职的指导老师，获得针对性的咨询服务。就业指导咨询服务包括掌握规划技能、探索就业前景、明确求职意向、了解行业企业、挖掘自身优势、修改中英文简历、装备面试技巧、推荐全职实习岗位等。

 就业实习信息发布：除了定期通过学校邮箱、社交媒体推送在线招聘岗位以外，我校就业信息服务平台会实时发布岗位信息。每年9-11月，每周举办至少5场企业宣讲会；每年举办两次大规模校园招聘会。

title: 2019 宁诺夏校 精彩回顾
content:
7月21日至27日，一批来自全国各地的高中生来到宁波诺丁汉大学参加夏校，体验为期一周的沉浸式英式课堂。本次夏校共有60名高中生参加，他们来自吉林、辽宁、北京、天津、河北、山东、陕西、河南、江苏、四川、重庆、湖北、浙江、江西、福建、海南等全国16个省市。同学们在体验英式教育的同时，还结交了一群来自五湖四海的朋友。

From July 21st to 27th, a group of high school students around China came to University of Nottingham Ningbo China (UNNC) to attend the summer school. There are 60 participants and they are from 16 provinces and municipalities (26 cities). While experiencing the British education, the students also made friends from all over the country.


在这为期一周的夏校生活中，同学们从学术课程和课外活动两方面深度体验了宁诺的多元文化和教育环境，实地了解宁诺各学院及专业设置，与中外师生开展了丰富的文化交流。

During the one-week study, the students had multicultural  experience at UNNC from both academic courses and outdoor activities, got to know the University faculties and majors and had communications with students and teachers from all over the world.

来自宁诺英语语言教学中心、人文社科学院、理工学院和商学院的多位老师热情风趣，为学员们带去了丰富多彩的课堂体验。学员们深刻感受到宁诺对培养学生批判性思维、创新性思维和团队合作意识的重视，也对日后的理想专业有了更为清晰的认识。

Tutors from Center for English Language Education, Faculty of Humanities and Social Sciences, Faculty of Business and Faculty of Science and Enginnering delivered courses for summer school students and guided them to understand the significance of critical thinking, innovation and group work. Through the one-week study, students had a clearer understanding of choosing major in the future.


英语写作与赏析和英语听力与会话

An Introduction to Writing at University and an Introduction to Lecture Listening and Academic Discussions

丰富的课外活动也给同学们留下了美好的回忆——毛毡油画体验，同学们用自己的作品致敬名画《星空》；博物馆参观，同学们感受到了宁波深厚的历史文化积淀；凯利舞会，同学们体验了苏格兰的传统舞蹈；俱乐部活动，同学们在健身房球场挥洒汗水；飞盘体验，同学们在落日余晖下看着飞盘划过天空；攀岩活动，同学们克服恐惧勇攀高峰。

Various activities left great impression on participants as well.
In the Wool Felt Oil Painting course, the students used their works to pay tribute to the famous painting "Starry Sky" by Van Gogh; when visiting the Ningbo Museum, the students felt the profound culture of Ningbo; at the Ceilidh Dancing party, the students experienced the traditional dance in Scotland. They sweated in the gym, played  Frisbee, and went climbing. The whole campus was immersed in cheerful laughter and happiness.

生日惊喜
Four students were greatly surprised by the birthday party we prepared for them.





在最后的汇报演出暨结业典礼中，同学们用精彩的表演为本次夏校活动画上了完美的句点。

In the final performance and graduation ceremony, students ended up the summer school with their wonderful performances.

关于宁波诺丁汉大学
宁波诺丁汉大学宣传片

宁波诺丁汉大学创建于 2004 年，是中国第一所经教育部批准引进世界一流大学（特指世界百强高校）并具有独立法人资格、独立校园的中外合作大学。大学目前有 8000 多名学生，其中大概 13% 的学生来自港澳台，以及 75 个国家和地区。


学校已建立商学院、人文与社会科学学院和理工学院三大学院，是全国第一所提供本科、硕士和博士多层次专业教学的中外合作大学。




截止至今日，我校已与遍布 30 多个国家和地区的约 100 所海外一流院校建立密切交流合作关系，保证每一位学生都有体验海外学习的机会。
